ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:10A:3.2.1.4
Title: 3.2.1.4 Audiology Therapy (Aural Rehabilitation)
Section: 3.2.1.4
Policy: 10A
Type: clinical_policy
Citation link: [Clinical Coverage Policy 10A](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/10a-outpatient-specialized-therapies/download?attachment)
Reason: Matched limitation.
Content:
Medicaid shall cover medically necessary audiology services when the beneficiary demonstrates the following:
the presence of any degree or type of hearing loss on the basis of the results of an audiologic (aural) rehabilitation evaluation; or
the presence of impaired or compromised auditory processing abilities based on the results of a central auditory test battery.
A beneficiary shall have one or more of the following deficits to initiate therapy:
hearing loss (any type) with a pure tone average greater than 25dB in either ear;
Standard Score more than one SD (standard deviation) below normal for chronological age on standardized tests of language, audition, speech, or auditory processing which must be documented on the basis of the results of a central auditory test battery; or
less than 1-year gain in skills (auditory, speech, processing) during a period of 12-calendar months.
Aural rehabilitation consists of:
facilitating receptive and expressive communication of a beneficiary with hearing loss;
achieving improved, augmented or compensated communication processes;
improving auditory processing, listening, spoken language processing, auditory memory, overall communication process; and
benefiting learning and daily activities.
Evaluation for aural rehabilitation
Service delivery requires ALL the following elements:
The provider shall check the functioning of hearing aids, assistive listening systems and devices, and sensory aids prior to the evaluation.
Through interview, observation, and clinical testing, the provider shall evaluate the beneficiary's skills, in both clinical and natural environments, for the following:
medical and audiological history;
reception, comprehension, and production of language in oral, or manual language modalities;
speech and voice production;
perception of speech and non-speech stimuli in multiple modalities;
listening skills;
speech-reading; and
communication strategies.
The provider shall determine the specific functional limitation(s), which must be measurable, for the beneficiary.
Evaluation for Central Auditory Processing Disorders (CAPD)
CAPD evaluation is to be completed by an audiologist and consists of tests to evaluate the beneficiary's overall auditory function. Through interview, observation, and clinical testing, the provider shall evaluate the beneficiary for ALL the following:
Communication, medical, and educational history;
Medicaid shall cover the following Central auditory tests for the identification of CAPD:
auditory discrimination test;
auditory temporal processing and patterning test;
 dichotic speech test;
 monaural low-redundancy speech test;
binaural interaction test;
 electroacoustic measures; and
electrophysiologic measures.
Interpretation of evaluations are derived from the beneficiary's performance on multiple tests. The diagnosis of CAPD must be based on a score of two standard deviations below the mean on at least two central auditory tests.
The provider shall determine the specific functional limitation(s), which must be measurable, for the beneficiary.
Functional deficits consist of  a beneficiary's inability to:
hear normal conversational speech;
hear conversation via the telephone;
identify, by hearing, environmental sounds necessary for safety (such as siren, car horn, doorbell, baby crying);
understand conversational speech (in person or via telephone);
hear and understand teacher in classroom setting;
hear and understand classmates during class discussion;
hear and understand co-workers or supervisors during meetings at work;
hear and process the super-segmental aspects of speech or the phonemes of speech; or
localize sound.
Language therapy treatment sessions must not be billed concurrently with aural rehabilitation therapy treatment sessions.
Note : This policy does not address postoperative diagnostic analysis and programming of cochlear and auditory brainstem implant services performed by licensed audiologists. For coverage criteria for these services, refer to Clinical Coverage Policy 1A-4, Cochlear and Auditory Brainstem Implants , found on NC Medicaid's website https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/

per_question.question: A CAP/DA participant wants to switch to a different service provider. Is that allowed, and what rules apply when an eligible beneficiary transfers?
per_question.agent_answer:
Yes. A CAP/DA beneficiary may change providers, and the policy protects the beneficiary’s right to choose among Medicaid-enrolled providers as part of the person-centered service plan process.

If the beneficiary wants to change the case management entity (CME), the beneficiary may request transfer to another approved case management provider, but the current CME must complete a root cause analysis within five business days to protect the beneficiary’s health and well-being, identify utilization limits, and assess the newly selected CME, and NC Medicaid must approve the transfer of CME.

If the transfer involves moving to another county or another entity, the CME must coordinate the transfer on the agreed transition date or within 30 calendar days of the request to transfer.

Before the transfer happens, the CME must coordinate the transfer to prevent gaps in services and complete these steps: determine the anticipated start date of services; coordinate a transition plan between provider agencies; discuss and plan for the beneficiary’s health, safety, and well-being; transfer the electronic health record in the CAP Business System; arrange a home visit by the receiving entity within five business days after the move to assess the new home environment and identify health and welfare concerns; and coordinate services to begin on the first day of the transfer.

For a CAP/DA beneficiary transferring to a different county specifically, the transferring and receiving CME designees must coordinate the transfer together, discuss health and safety planning, transfer the electronic health record, arrange the receiving-county home visit within five business days of the move, and plan for services to start on the first transfer date into the receiving county.

A beneficiary who is already approved for CAP/DA remains eligible after transferring to another county, and county residence does not end CAP/DA participation. Ongoing Medicaid eligibility is checked at the next Medicaid certification period.

If there is a waitlist in the transferring county, a transferring CAP/DA beneficiary is treated as a priority category and is guaranteed a slot immediately in the receiving county.

Any CAP/DA services that continue after transfer still must be provided in the type, amount, duration, and frequency authorized in the approved CAP/DA service plan, and providers may not bill beyond what is authorized unless the unplanned occurrence criteria is met.

The current CAP/DA policy was revised effective 2025-09-01, and the change notice states that all sections and attachments were revised to align with the CMS-approved CAP/DA renewal waiver effective 11/01/2024.

If you want, I can also turn this into a short advocate checklist for requesting a provider or CME transfer.

---

*Suggested citations for uncited claims above:*
- [Policy 3K-2 § 5.4.2](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)
- [Policy 3K-2 § 3.3](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)
- [Policy 3K-2 CAP/DA Claim Reimbursement](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)
- [Policy 3K-2 Revision — 2025-09-01](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)

It correctly identifies that CAP/DA beneficiaries may change providers, accurately describes the root cause analysis requirement within five business days for CME transfers, the 30-calendar-day coordination timeline, the pre-transfer steps (determining start date, transition plan, health/safety planning, EHR transfer, home visit within 5 business days, service start on first transfer date), county transfer rules, continued eligibility regardless of county, Medicaid eligibility at next certification period, priority category/guaranteed slot when waitlist is active, and billing constraints. All these facts are directly supported by the Evidence block (sections 3.3, COORDINATION OF CARE section, 3.2.4, and CAP/DA Claim Reimbursement). The 2025-09-01 amendment reference is also supported by the getAmendments evidence. No hallucinations are present. Citation quality is good but not perfect — the agent provides section-level citations (§5.4.2, §3.3, CAP/DA Claim Reimbursement, 2025-09-01 revision) but lists them as 'suggested citations' at the end rather than inline, and misses citing the COORDINATION OF CARE section for the root cause analysis detail. Overall, a Medicaid policy expert would find this answer thorough and accurate.

ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:3K-2:_s256
Title: CAP IN-HOME AIDE II SERVICE
Policy: 3K-2
Type: clinical_policy
Citation link: [Community Alternatives Program for Disabled Adults (CAP/DA)](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)
Reason: Matched cap/da.
Content:
This is a service for a CAP/DA beneficiary who is unable to perform any two of the seven key Activities of Daily Living (ADLs) tasks independently due to a medical condition identified and documented on a validated assessment. This service provides limited to extensive hands-on assistance (not merely set-up or cueing) with or monitoring of at least two ADLs (bathing, dressing, eating, toileting, hygiene, mobility and transferring). At least one of the ADLs must be Nurse Aide I task or greater during the hours of service provision. The need for assistance with ADLs relates directly to the CAP/DA beneficiary's physical, social environmental and functional condition. Nurse Aide Services, when medically necessary, must be provided in the community, home, workplace, or educational settings (when not the responsibility of LEA).
A CAP/DA beneficiary approved for In-Home Aide II have task needs at Level III, which requires substantial ADL support with health and personal care tasks. Involves extensive 'hands on' care and assistance with oxygen therapy, break-up and removal of fecal impaction, sterile dressing change, wound irrigation, I.V. fluid assistive activities, nutrition activities, suctioning, tracheostomy care, elimination procedures and urinary catheters. Level III tasks are considered higher-level tasks for CAP/DA. Lower level tasks are Level I tasks, home management such as housekeeping, cooking, shopping, and bill
paying; and Level II tasks, assistance with basic activities of daily living (e.g., eating, dressing, bathing, etc.) and home management tasks can be provided in addition to Level III tasks.
This service type is substantial. The CAP/DA beneficiary care needs must fall within the NA I scope of nursing practice or greater, per the North Carolina Board of Nursing. The staff providing the care must be NA II or the Home Health agency shall have competencies for NA I + 4 tasks, unless participation in the CAP/DA is through consumer direction.
Other Level I tasks include paying bills as directed by the CAP/DA beneficiary; essential shopping, cleaning and caring for clothing; performing basic housekeeping tasks such as sweeping, vacuuming, dusting, mopping and washing dishes; identifying medications for the CAP/DA beneficiary; providing companionship and emotional support; preparing simple meals; and shopping for food, clothes, and other essential items.
Nurse Aide services shall not be provided by personal care aides or home health aides not registered with DHSR, unless participation in the CAP/DA is through consumer direction.
The beneficiary must have a caregiver available to provide needed services during the planned and unplanned absences of the nurse aide. If the regular informal caregiver is not available; there must be a back-up informal caregiver designated who can be physically present with the beneficiary and make judgments on the caregiver's behalf regarding the care of the beneficiary.
The supervising registered nurse of the provider agency maintains accountability and responsibility for the delivery of safe and competent care (NC Board of Nursing). Decisions regarding the delegation of any nurse aide tasks are made by the licensed nurse on a beneficiary-by-beneficiary basis.
The criteria stated below must be met in order for a task to be delegated to unlicensed personnel:
is performed frequently in the daily care of a beneficiary or group of beneficiaries;
is performed according to an established sequence of steps;
involves little or no modification from one beneficiary situation to another;
may be performed with a predictable outcome;
does not involve ongoing assessment, interpretation, or decision-making that cannot be logically separated from the task itself; and
does not endanger the beneficiary's life or well-being.
Tasks, amount, frequency, and duration must be clearly outlined in job duties developed by the CAP beneficiary or responsible party or representative participating in consumer direction care.
Short-term intensive services are eligible to be used with this service. Short-term intensive services are used for a significant change in the acuity status of the CAP beneficiary where the duration of care needs is less than three consecutive weeks. Short-term intensive services are listed in the service plan. Shortterm-intensive care is used to approve extra hours that are needed due to a change in the beneficiary's condition resulting in additional or increased medical needs or a caregiver crisis (significant illness or death in the family).
Unplanned CAP/DA service occurrence requests are eligible to be used with this service. Unplanned CAP/DA services occurrence requests are used to request an adjustment beyond the approved CAP/DA service for a particular day(s) due to an unexpected event.
A CAP/DA beneficiary can use up to 14 days per year of recreational leave, when planned for in the initial and annual person-centered service plan. The exact dates of the leave do not have to be documented in the service plan when the initial or annual plan is completed.
Assistance from the nurse aide when traveling out of state is allowed when the provision of this service complies with NCBON licensure and certification rules, the service plan and clinical coverage policy 2A3, Out-of-State Services .
Nurse Aide services, when medically necessary, shall be provided in the home, community, and workplace when identified as person-centered goals in the service plan.
Nurse Aide services are subject to the EVV requirements, and the provider agency shall comply with Section 12006 1903(l) of the 21st Century Cures Act and any subsequent amendments, when applicable.
A paid live-in caregiver is excluded from the EVV requirements. The provider agency must attest that the paid live-in caregiver assigned to the CAP/DA beneficiary meets the definition of a paid live-in caregiver to be excluded from capturing EVV data, refer to Appendix F. An attestation must be completed initially and

ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:3K-2:_s252
Title: CAP / DA IN-HOME AIDE I SERVICE
Policy: 3K-2
Type: clinical_policy
Citation link: [Community Alternatives Program for Disabled Adults (CAP/DA)](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)
Reason: Matched cap/da.
Content:
In-home aide service is a range of assistance to enable CAP/DA beneficiaries to accomplish tasks that they would normally do for themselves if they did not have a disability. This assistance may take the form of hands-on assistance (actually performing a task for the person) or cueing to prompt the beneficiary to perform a task, supervision of a task, or monitoring. In-home aide services may be provided on an episodic or on a continuing basis. In-home aide services may provide limited to greater assistance with or monitoring of a minimum of two Activities of Daily Living (ADLs) and basic home management tasks when documented in the comprehensive assessment that evaluates physical, social, environmental, and functional condition. Support, monitor, supervision, and assistance are provided for seven keys ADLs: bathing, dressing, eating, toileting, hygiene, mobility and transfer, and key Instrumental Activities of Daily Living (IADLs) to include: light housework, laundry, meal preparation, transportation, grocery shopping, using the telephone, medication, and money management).  Such assistance also may include the supervision of beneficiaries as provided in the service plan.
In-home aide service needs must fall within the Nurse Aide I scope of nursing practice or greater, per the North Carolina Board of Nursing.  In-home aide services may be provided in the community, home, workplace, or educational settings at the discretion of the Home Care Agency. In-home aide services can be provided in the workplace for CAP/DA beneficiaries who meet the specified qualifications.  A beneficiary approved for In-home aide can receive services at any of the task levels as described below. Level I tasks consists of home management tasks such as housekeeping, cooking, shopping, and bill paying. Level II tasks are assistance with basic activities of daily living (e.g., eating, dressing, bathing, etc.) and home management tasks. Higher-level tasks are Level III tasks, and they are oxygen therapy, break-up and removal of fecal impaction, sterile dressing change, wound irrigation, I.V. fluid assistive activities, nutrition activities, suctioning, tracheostomy care, elimination procedures and urinary catheters. Level III tasks are substantial and involves extensive 'hands on' care and assistance with a wide range of health-related conditions. Other Level I tasks include paying bills as directed by the beneficiary; essential shopping, cleaning and caring for clothing; performing basic housekeeping tasks such as sweeping, vacuuming, dusting, mopping and washing dishes; identifying medications for the beneficiary; providing companionship and emotional support; preparing simple meals; and shopping for food, clothes, and other essential items.
Personal care under the waiver differs in scope, nature, supervision arrangements, and provider type (including provider training and qualifications) from personal care services in the State plan.
The In-Home aide needs must fall within the NA I scope of nursing practice or greater.
Tasks, amount, frequency, and duration must be clearly outlined in job duties developed by the CAP/DA beneficiary, responsible party or representative.
Short-term intensive services may be used under this service. Short-term intensive services are used for a change in the status of the CAP/DA beneficiary where the duration of care needs is less than three weeks. Short-term intensive services  are contained in the service plan.
A CAP/DA beneficiary can use up to 14 days per year of recreational leave, when planned for in the initial and annual person-centered service plan. The exact dates of the leave do not have to be included in the service plan when the initial or annual plan is completed.
Assistance from this service when traveling out of state is allowed when the provision of this service complies with BON- licensure and certification rules.
An assigned worker may accompany a CAP/DA beneficiary and the primary caregiver to a medical appointment, to and from school or other activities, if documented in the service plan to provide medical care or personal assistance for the CAP/DA beneficiary.
ADL care for adults under the Medicaid Infrastructure Grant (MIG) with Vocational Rehabilitation can be provided in the workplace for a CAP/DA  beneficiary who qualifies.
Tasks, amount, frequency, and duration must be clearly outlined in job duties developed by the CAP/DA beneficiary or responsible party/representative.
Individuals with the following criminal records are excluded from hire:
Felonies related to manufacture, distribution, prescription, or dispensing of a controlled substance;
More than one felony conviction related to healthcare fraud;
Felony for abuse, neglect, assault, battery, criminal sexual conduct (1st, 2nd or 3rd degree), fraud or theft against a minor or vulnerable adult;
Felony or misdemeanor patient abuse;
Felony or misdemeanor involving cruelty or torture;
Misdemeanor healthcare fraud;
Misdemeanor for abuse, neglect, or exploitation of a minor or disabled adult;
Substantiated allegation of abuse, neglect or exploitation listed with the NC Health Care Registry; or
Any substantiated allegation listed with the NC Health Care Registry that would prohibit an individual from working in the health care field in the state of NC.
Note: Individuals with criminal offenses occurring more than 10 years previous may qualify for an exemption. The exemption approval must be agreed upon by the CAP/DA beneficiary and documented in the case files.
Note: Individuals directing their own care must comply with the US Department of Labor Fair Labor Standards Act.
CAP In-Home Aide service is subject to the EVV requirements, and the provider agency shall comply with Section 12006 1903(l) of the 21st Century Cures Act and any subsequent amendments, when applicable.

ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:3K-2:_s211
Title: CAP/DA Claim Reimbursement
Policy: 3K-2
Type: clinical_policy
Citation link: [Community Alternatives Program for Disabled Adults (CAP/DA)](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)
Reason: Matched cap/da.
Content:
The Case Management Entity (CME) may bill for case management services, equipment, modification and technology, training and education services, community transition services, community integration services goods and services, according to this policy, their own agency policy, and NCTracks Provider Claims and Billing Assistance Guide :
https://www.nctracks.nc.gov/content/public/providers/provider-manuals.html
Approved CAP/DA providers shall bill for adult day health, financial management, In-Home aide, equipment, modification and technology, meal preparation and delivery, specialized medical supplies and personal emergency response, respite and when authorized training and education services, community transition services, community integration services goods and services service according to Subsection 5.8 , their own agency policy and NCTracks Provider Claims and Billing Assistance Guide :
https://www.nctracks.nc.gov/content/public/providers/provider-manuals.html
Provider(s) subject to the EVV requirements shall capture and verify seven (7) core in-home visit components, which are required under the 21st Century Cures Act to complete real-time electronic verification, tracking, and documentation. These core components are:
Date of Service;
Location of service delivery;
Individual providing service;
Type of services performed;
Individual receiving service;
Time service begins; and
Time service ends.
The qualifying services to be validated are listed below:
S5125 - In-home aide services I
S5125 UN - Congregate In-home aide services
S5150 - In-home respite care
S5135- Personal Assistance Services
S5135 UN - Congregate personal assistance services
T1019 - In-home aide services II
T1004 - In-home aide services II respite
The provider(s) submitting a claim for a paid live-in caregiver must attest using a Paid Live-in Caregiver Attestation Form the caregiver meets the live-in status definition to allow the claim to bypass the EVV edits using place of service (POS) 99, refer to Appendix F.
CAP/DA services are provided by the type, amount, duration, and frequency, consistent with the CAP/DA beneficiary's medical needs and must be provided according to the service authorization. The amount of service provided cannot exceed what is contained in the approved CAP/DA service plan, unless the unplanned occurrence criteria is met. A provider shall not bill for a service if the procedure is not valid for the CAP/DA benefit program, or if the policies and procedures relevant to that service were not adhered to. CAP/DA providers shall not file a claim for a beneficiary who is ineligible for CAP/DA services.
A request for payment for an assessment of an individual who does not become a CAP/DA beneficiary can be made if all of the following conditions are met:
The individual has a properly approved SRF.
The assessment was completed according to CAP/DA policies, procedures and timelines.
The assessment is documented and certified by the assessment multidisciplinary team on the CAP/DA assessment form.
The individual is notified in writing of the reason they cannot enroll in the CAP/DA.
A claim for the assessment of an individual who does not be participating in CAP/DA is called an 'assessment only' claim. The claim is paid directly by NC Medicaid instead of through NCTracks. To submit an 'assessment only' claim:
Prepare a paper claim for the service
Prepare a cover letter that includes:
The Individual's name and Medicaid ID number; and
The reason the individual cannot participate in CAP/DA.
A beneficiary in a facility (nursing home or hospital) shall receive CAP/DA services on the date of admission and the date of discharge. Specific CAP/DA services can be provided prior to 30 or 60 calendar days of a discharge from a facility placement when the CAP/DA services assist with transitional planning. An individual in an institutional setting may be authorized to use home and community-based services to assist with the transition to a more independent and less restrictive living arrangement. Certain CAP/DA services such as community transition and specific modification services may be furnished in advance of the discharge of the person from the institutional setting.  All transition and modification services must be reasonable and necessary, not available to the CAP/DA applicant through other means, clearly specified in a discharge or transition plan, and subsequently carried over to the CAP/DA service plan resulting in a prior approval. Billing for these approved services is available once the CAP evidence code is entered into the Medicaid system.

ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:3K-2:5.4.2:dup1
Title: 5.4.2 CAP/DA Person-Centered Service Plan Requirements
Section: 5.4.2
Policy: 3K-2
Type: clinical_policy
Citation link: [Community Alternatives Program for Disabled Adults (CAP/DA)](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)
Reason: Matched cap/da.
Content:
The service plan approval date is assigned after an approved assessment. The effective date of the service plan is the first day of the next eligible month or the first day of the next eligible month after approval of Medicaid eligibility, if Medicaid eligibility is not established before the CAP approval date.
The initial service plan must be completed within 30 calendar days of the assignment to the Case Management Entity (CME).
The CME shall work closely with the applicant or beneficiary to develop an initial or annual person-centered service plan based on the needs identified in the comprehensive assessment. A person-centered service plan allows the applicant or beneficiary to identify preferences, likes and dislikes to create a care plan of both formal and informal supports. The completed person-centered plan contains a plan of care (POC) that lists all approved CAP/DA and Medicaid State Plan services in the type, amount, frequency and duration. The annual average per capita cost for these services shall be listed in the POC to evaluate the annual cost of care needs.
The CME uses the service plan to achieve the following:
Summarize the evaluation and assessment information to highlight the beneficiary's strengths and needs;
Outline person-centered goals and objectives based on the assessment and identified needs;
Develop a comprehensive list of CAP/DA waiver services and non-waiver services, medical supplies and durable medical equipment (DME), and document the authorized provider name, amount, frequency and duration of each service;
Calculate the monthly beneficiary cost of care for all CAP/DA waiver services and State Plan services.
Ensure the beneficiary's right to choose among providers as evidenced by a signed freedom of choice form;
Ensure the beneficiary's right to choose between CAP/DA, institutionalization, and from among Medicaid-enrolled providers as evidenced by a signed Freedom of Choice form;
Identify health and welfare monitoring priorities during the mandatory monthly and quarterly timelines; and
Soliciting the agreement through a signature from the CAP/DA beneficiary that the service plan meets the assessed needs in the type, amount, frequency and duration.
Note: The annual service plan must be approved by the first day of the month following the Continued Need Review (CNR) assessment.

ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:3K-2:6.1
Title: 6.1 Provider Qualifications and Occupational Licensing Entity Regulations
Section: 6.1
Policy: 3K-2
Type: clinical_policy
Citation link: [Community Alternatives Program for Disabled Adults (CAP/DA)](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)
Reason: Matched documentation.
Content:
Medicaid providers seeking to provide CAP/DA services shall meet all requirements for provider enrollment established by DHHS fiscal contractor and have an approved managed change request for specific taxonomies listed in the CAP benefit plan. Each selected Medicaid provider of CAP/DA services shall undergo a CAP/DA overview and orientation training prior to rendering authorized services, and annually thereafter.
Federally Recognized Tribes are eligible to provide all CAP/DA services when the following items are met:
Any requirement under a Federal health care program that a provider as defined in G.S. 108C-2(10) be licensed or recognized under the State or local law where the provider is located shall be deemed to have been met:
When a provider entity is operated by the Service, an Indian tribe, tribal organization, or urban Indian organization; and
If the provider entity meets all applicable standards for such licensure or recognition.
The licensure or recognition shall be deemed to have been met regardless of whether the entity obtains a license or other documentation under State or local law.
NC Medicaid requires the following supervision to be performed as listed:
Supervision of the CNA minimally every 90 calendar days, in the home, by the RN Supervisor.
The following types of staff provide CAP/DA waiver services:
Certified Nursing Assistant I;
Certified Nursing Assistant II;
Personal assistant for consumer-directed care; or
Live-in caregiver for coordinated caregiving services.
Providers(s) shall comply with Section 12006(l) (Electronic Visit Verification {EVV}) of the 21 st Century Cures Act and any subsequent amendments to validate in-home visit(s) rendered for personal care type services approved in this policy.
Providers of in-home aide and personal assistance services to the CAP/DA beneficiary shall:
have written documentation that recipients of in-home aide and personal assistance services were informed of the EVV requirement;
complete all required EVV trainings prior to providing in-home aide and personal assistance services;
train staff on use of selected EVV system; and
ensure administrator, essential personnel and staff within an organization participate in initial EVV training; and annual and refresher training in EVV, when applicable.
The CAP/DA Direct Service provider shall provide a copy of the agency policies and procedures that identify the assurance of nonuse of restraints and seclusion and critical incident management.
The CAP/DA Direct and Coordinated Caregiving service providers shall attest that hired workers have a criminal history and health care registry check free from the offenses found in Appendix B prior to rendering CAP/DA services.

ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:3K-2:_s244
Title: COORDINATION OF CARE: CASE MANAGEMENT AND CARE ADVISEMENT
Policy: 3K-2
Type: clinical_policy
Citation link: [Community Alternatives Program for Disabled Adults (CAP/DA)](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)
Reason: Matched order.
Content:
A service that directs and manages the special health care, social, environmental, financial and emotional needs of a CAP/DA beneficiary in order to maintain the beneficiary's health, safety, and well-being and for continual community integration.
The Case Management Entity (CME) shall retain the following documents:
Service Request Form (SRF);
all assessments;
service plan;
d.
case management notes;
service authorizations;
copies of claims generated by the case management entity;
any required documents generated by other providers and approved by the case management entity; and
related correspondence in compliance with all applicable federal and state laws, rules and regulations.
Case management is a CAP/DA service offered to a CAP/DA beneficiary to assist in navigating community systems and gaining access to Medicaid services to meet their identified needs. The comprehensive interdisciplinary assessment identifies the lack of an informal support system and the need for intervention by a case manager. When the assessment identifies a CAP/DA beneficiary to be at risk of institutionalization, case management must be listed in the service plan on a monthly basis. The CAP/DA beneficiary has the option to select an approved case management provider, which is the sole case management provider for that CAP/DA beneficiary. If a request is made to transfer to another case management entity, a root cause analysis must be performed within five business days to assure the health and well-being of the CAP/DA beneficiary, as well as to identify utilization limits and assess the performance of the newly selected case management entity. NC Medicaid shall approve the transfer of CME.
There are two types of case managers under case management and four principles of case management (listed below):
The two types of case managers are:
Case Manager provides services for a CAP/DA beneficiary participating in provider-led services.
Care Advisor provides specialized case management to a CAP/DA beneficiary participating in consumer-directed care. The care advisor focuses on empowering beneficiary to define and direct their own personal assistance needs and services. The care advisor guides and supports the CAP/DA beneficiary, rather than directs and manages the CAP/DA beneficiary, throughout the service planning and delivery process. These functions are done under the guidance and direction of the CAP beneficiary or responsible party.
There are Four Principle Activities of Case Management:
Assessment
Care planning
Referral and Linkage
Monitoring & Follow-up
When the case management entity is authorized to be the 'HCBS passthrough provider' to ensure access to needed services as identified in an approved plan of care (POC), the case management entity can develop a one-time purchase order for the obtainment of the approved waiver item by giving the beneficiary a check made out to the provider.
The provider must provide an invoice to the case management entity within 15 business days. A second option a case management entity can use is to set up a purchase account at a retailer. The beneficiary and provider must sign an invoice to validate obtaining the approved waiver items.
A third option that can be used is online purchases using a VISA card. Each beneficiary is assigned their own VISA card if online purchasing is approved. Funds are loaded to the VISA card when a waiver item is approved. The funds can only be loaded to the VISA card when a waiver service is approved. The exact amount of the approved waiver item can only be loaded onto the card. The beneficiary is given a VISA gift card. The case manager documents the VISA account number and associated pin in the beneficiary's record to assist with loading funds for future approved waiver items.

ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:3K-2:3.3
Title: 3.3 Transfers of Eligible Beneficiaries
Section: 3.3
Policy: 3K-2
Type: clinical_policy
Citation link: [Community Alternatives Program for Disabled Adults (CAP/DA)](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)
Reason: Matched provider.
Content:
When a transfer request is received, by the Case Management Entity (CME), the CME shall coordinate the transfer of an eligible CAP/DA beneficiary to another county or entity within the approved, agreed upon transition date or less than 30 calendar days of the request to transfer.
CME shall coordinate the transfer to prevent gaps in service provisions. The following steps must be completed prior to the transfer:
determine anticipated start date of service;
coordinate transition plan between provider agencies;
discuss and plan for the health, safety and well-being of the beneficiary;
initiate in the CAP Business System (e-CAP/DA) the transfer of the electronic health records to the receiving county;
arrange for a home visit within five (5) business days of the date the CAP/DA beneficiary moves to their new primary residence by the receiving entity to assess the home environment identifying any health and welfare concerns and planning for mitigation and safety; and
coordinate and plan the provision of services to start on the first date of the transfer.
For a CAP/C beneficiary aging out of CAP/C and wishes to transfer to CAP/DA:
The CAP/C CME designee shall implement a transition, transfer plan 12 months prior to the birth month. These coordination activities are:
Completion of a transition plan during the annual needs review assessment that occurs at age 20; and
Consultation with the CAP/C beneficiary and primary caregiver to educate about other Medicaid and community resources to meet needs after the age of 21.
Three months (90 calendar days) prior to the birth month or identified transfer month, a multidisciplinary team meeting must be convened to discuss care needs and to ensure the identified formal and informal resources are able to meet care needs.
The month prior to the birth month, the local DSS must be notified of the need to change the CAP evidence code for CAP/DA participation for the identified CAP/DA effective start date.
On the first day of the birth month or identified transfer month, CAP/DA services are authorized and provided to the beneficiary.
Note: A Service Request Form (SFR) is not required. An assessment is required to identify ongoing adult needs for the generation of an adult service plan.
For a CAP/DA beneficiary transferring to a different county:
The CME designee of the transferring agency shall coordinate the transfer with the CME designee of the receiving agency upon the agreed upon transfer date or less than 30 calendar days of the request to transfer.
The CME designee of the transferring and receiving agencies shall discuss and plan for the health, safety and well-being of the beneficiary.
The electronic health record is transferred to the receiving county.
The CME designee of the receiving agency shall arrange for a home visit within five (5) business days of the date the CAP/DA beneficiary moves in their new primary residence to assess the environment to identify any health and welfare concerns to plan for mitigation and safety.
The CME designee shall coordinate and plan the provision of services to start on the first date of the transfer into the receiving county.
Note: An active beneficiary previously approved to participate in CAP/DA can continue to participate in the program when a transfer to another county occurs. A transferring beneficiary continues to be eligible for CAP/DA regardless of their county of residence.  Ongoing Medicaid eligibility is determined at the next Medicaid certification period.
When a waitlist is active in the transferring county, the CAP/DA beneficiary is considered in a priority category and guaranteed a slot immediately in the receiving county.

ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:3K-2:6.5
Title: 6.5 Medicaid Provider Requirement to Provide CAP/DA Waiver Services
Section: 6.5
Policy: 3K-2
Type: clinical_policy
Citation link: [Community Alternatives Program for Disabled Adults (CAP/DA)](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)
Reason: Matched provider.
Content:
Qualified NC Medicaid providers are granted approval to render CAP services through a managed change request.  Providers are approved based on their approved Medicaid provider application and their qualifying taxonomies. Each qualified provider must adhere to the following when selected to render a CAP/DA service:
register as a user of the CAP Business System (e-CAP) and participate in required trainings.
accept, decline, or acknowledge service authorizations within three (3) business days of submission in the e-CAP system.
complete a CAP/DA overview and orientation training prior to rendering authorized services, and annually thereafter for updates and refresher of CAP/DA policies.
attest to having policies and procedures that identifies the assurance of nonuse of restraints and seclusions and critical incident management.
attest that hired workers successfully pass a background check that includes a health care registry.
comply with Section 12006 1903(l) of the 21st Century Cures Act and any subsequent amendments, when applicable.

per_question.question: For Health Coverage for Workers with Disabilities: is there a ceiling on how much a person can earn from work and still qualify, and do enrollees have to pay premiums?
per_question.agent_answer:
Yes — for [unverified: earned work income, the surfaced HCWD policy does not set a hard earnings ceiling; instead, HCWD uses income levels to determine eligibility and cost-sharing, and the policy says the only explicit eligibility cap in the surfaced text is that people with unearned income greater than 150% of FPL are not eligible.] [Policy MA-2180 § F. Income](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/ma-2180-3.pdf) The 2014 HCWD Phase III change notice likewise says MA-2180 was revised “to remove limits on countable income except for the 150% of Federal Poverty Level (FPL) cap on unearned income.” [unverified quote — not found in retrieved sources] [Policy Change Notice 01-14](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/ma_cn01-14.pdf)

Yes — some enrollees do have to pay premiums. [Policy MA-2180 § I. Premiums](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/ma-2180-3.pdf) The policy says people with total countable monthly income above 150% of FPL must pay a $50 enrollment fee for each 12-month certification period. [Policy MA-2180 § H. Enrollment Fee](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/ma-2180-3.pdf)

The policy also says people with total countable monthly income above 200% of FPL must pay a monthly premium in addition to that $50 yearly enrollment fee. [Policy MA-2180 § F. Income](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/ma-2180-3.pdf) [Policy MA-2180 § I. Premiums](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/ma-2180-3.pdf)

The premium rises as income rises, and once countable income is above 450% of FPL, the person owes a 100% premium. [Policy MA-2180 § F. Income](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/ma-2180-3.pdf) [Policy MA-2180 § I. Premiums](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/ma-2180-3.pdf)

Members of federally recognized Native American tribes and Alaska Natives are exempt from cost sharing, including enrollment fees and premiums. [Policy MA-2180 § H. Enrollment Fee](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/ma-2180-3.pdf)

The current MA-2180 document is marked “Revised 2/3/2025 – Change No. 03-25,” [unverified quote — not found in retrieved sources] and the amendment history says Change Notice 03-25 updated the HCWD premium income chart. ID: sec:doc:dhhs_policy:MA-2180:url-08aa92cd33e7:_s1
Title: I. Introduction to Health Coverage for Workers with Disabilities
Policy: MA-2180
Type: dhhs_policy
Citation link: [MA-2180 HEALTH COVERAGE FOR WORKERS WITH DISABILITIES](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/ma-2180-3.pdf)
Reason: Matched introduction.
Content:
The federal Ticket to Work and Work Incentives Improvement Act (TWWIIA) of 1999 offers states the option to protect Medicaid coverage for workers with disabilities.  People with disabilities are often discouraged from working for fear that their earnings would make them ineligible for Medicaid.  TWWIIA offers state Medicaid programs options to expand Medicaid eligibility criteria for workers with disabilities.

ID: sec:doc:dhhs_policy:MA-2180:url-08aa92cd33e7:_s17
Title: H. Enrollment Fee
Policy: MA-2180
Type: dhhs_policy
Citation link: [MA-2180 HEALTH COVERAGE FOR WORKERS WITH DISABILITIES](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/ma-2180-3.pdf)
Reason: Income, fee, or premium section from the preferred HCWD document.
Content:
All individuals with total monthly countable income above 150% of the federal poverty level must pay a $50 enrollment fee for each twelve month certification period.  The enrollment fee is collected by the county and retained to offset administrative expenses.  Do not charge an enrollment fee for the retroactive month(s) when an a/b receives retroactive coverage.  If a premium is due (see II.C. below), the county must mail the enrollment fee notice with the premium invoice.
Note: Members of federally recognized Native American tribes and Alaska natives are exempt from cost sharing, including enrollment fees and premiums.

Supporting sections:
ID: sec:doc:dhhs_policy:url-11e0d9a442ce:_s6
Title: D.  MA-2180, Health Coverage for Workers with Disabilities, is revised in:
Type: dhhs_policy
Citation link: [CHANGE NOTICE FOR MANUAL NO. 01-14, HCWD Phase III](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/ma_cn01-14.pdf)
Reason: Matched health.
Content:
I., to remove references to federal Ticket to Work and Work Incentives Improvement Act (TWWIIA) grants;
II., to state that HCWD covers individuals regardless of total countable income or CAP status;
IV.B.2.b., to add the qualification that SSI was terminated 'for non-medical reasons' and use more recent dates in the example provided;
IV.D.1.a., clarify that work must be competitive and inclusive unless individual is self-employed;
IV.E., to remove limits on countable income except for the 150% of Federal Poverty Level (FPL) cap on unearned income and provide information about sliding scale premiums;
IV.G., to provide that those with countable incomes greater than 150% FPL must pay a $50 per certification period (yearly) enrollment fee. The enrollment fee is collected by the county and retained to offset administrative expenses;
IV.H., to state that those with countable incomes greater than 200% FPL must pay a premium in addition to an enrollment fee.  The premiums increase with income range until income exceeds 450% of FPL, at which point a 100% premium is due.  The 100% premium is based upon the average claims paid for an individual in the MAD and MAB programs;
Note:  All HCWD cases with income above 200% of FPL must be processed in EIS (see III. for EIS requirements).
IV.J., to remove the statement that retroactive coverage can begin no earlier than November 1, 2008;
IV.K., to correct the classification chart to read 'Greater than 100% FPL;'
IV.N., to state that the certification period for HCWD is 12 months;
V., to state that the certification period for HCWD is 12 months.

ID: sec:doc:dhhs_policy:MA-2180:url-08aa92cd33e7:_s15
Title: F. Income
Policy: MA-2180
Type: dhhs_policy
Citation link: [MA-2180 HEALTH COVERAGE FOR WORKERS WITH DISABILITIES](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/ma-2180-3.pdf)
Reason: Matched exclusion.
Content:
HCWD has varying income limits that will determine eligibility and/or cost sharing. These limits are:
Those who have unearned incomes greater than 150% of FPL are not eligible for HCWD.
Those whose total countable income is equal to or less than 150% of FPL have no cost sharing (other than applicable co-payments).
Those whose total countable income is greater than 150% of FPL must pay a $50 annual enrollment fee (see IV. G.).
Those whose total countable monthly income exceeds 200% of FPL must pay a monthly premium in addition to the enrollment fee.  The monthly premium increases as income increases until countable income exceeds 450% of FPL, at which point these individuals must pay a full premium (see IV.H. below). Because countable income determines whether the individual is subject to cost-sharing and the amount thereof, countable income must be determined and all applicable exclusions applied.
Note: These individuals are likely to have work expense exclusions for the blind and impairment-related work expense exclusions for the disabled.

ID: sec:doc:dhhs_policy:MA-2180:url-08aa92cd33e7:_s21
Title: I. Premiums
Policy: MA-2180
Type: dhhs_policy
Citation link: [MA-2180 HEALTH COVERAGE FOR WORKERS WITH DISABILITIES](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/ma-2180-3.pdf)
Reason: Income, fee, or premium section from the preferred HCWD document.
Content:
Individuals with countable income above 200% of FPL must pay a monthly premium in addition to an enrollment fee of $50 per year.  The premiums increase with income range until income exceeds 450% of FPL, at which point a 100% premium is due. The 100% premium is based upon the average claims paid for an individual receiving Medicaid and may change yearly.
The income ranges and associated premiums are found in the following chart:

| Federal Poverty Level   | IncomeRange-HCWD Individual   |   Monthly Premium | IncomeRange- HCWD Couple   |   Monthly Premium |
|:------------------------|:------------------------------|------------------:|:---------------------------|------------------:|
| 0-150%                  | $0 - 1,957                    |                 0 | $0 - 2,644                 |                 0 |
| 151-200%                | $1,957.01 - 2,609             |                 0 | $2,644.01 - 3,525          |                 0 |
| 201-250%                | $2,609.01 - 3,261             |               196 | $3,525.01 - 4,407          |               265 |
| 251-300%                | $3,261.01 - 3,913             |               235 | $4,407.01 - 5,288          |               318 |
| 301-350%                | $3,913.01 - 4,565             |               274 | $5,288.01 - 6,169          |               370 |
| 351-400%                | $4,565.01 - 5,217             |               313 | $6,169.01 - 7,050          |               423 |
| 401-450%                | $5,217.01 - 5,869             |               352 | $7,050.01 - 7,932          |               476 |
| 451and above            | $5,869.01 and up              |               875 | $7,932.01 and up           |               875 |

Individuals with countable income above 200% of FPL must pay a monthly premium in addition to an enrollment fee of $50 per year.  The premiums increase with income range until income exceeds 450% of FPL, at which point a 100% premium is due. The 100% premium is based upon the average claims paid for an individual receiving Medicaid and may change yearly.
The income ranges and associated premiums are found in the following chart:

per_question.question: Which federal statute lets North Carolina operate the CAP/DA waiver, and what does the state have to demonstrate to CMS in its waiver application?
per_question.agent_answer:
North Carolina operates CAP/DA under the federal [unverified: 1915(c) home- and community-based services waiver authority in the Social Security Act] . Section 1915(c) [unverified: allows the Secretary to waive normal state-plan requirements so a state may cover home- or community-based services, other than room and board, for people who would otherwise require institutional level of care in a hospital, nursing facility, or intermediate care facility].

## Federal rule: what CMS requires in the waiver application

A waiver request must include the assurances required by 42 CFR 441.302 and the supporting documentation required by 42 CFR 441.303.

If the state wants waiver of normal Medicaid statewideness, comparability, or certain community income/resource rules, the request must specifically ask for waiver of those requirements.

The state also must state whether it will refuse HCBS to a beneficiary when the agency reasonably expects the HCBS cost would exceed the cost of an equivalent level of institutional care in a hospital, nursing facility, or ICF/IID.

For an HCBS waiver application, the state must demonstrate that services will be furnished under a written, person-centered service plan approved by the Medicaid agency.

The application must show that services will be provided only to people who are not inpatients of a hospital, nursing facility, or ICF/IID, and only to people whom the state determines would otherwise require that Medicaid-covered level of care.

The state must describe who is qualified to develop the plan of care, which group or groups will be served, and what services will be furnished, with each service separately defined rather than open-ended or improperly bundled.

The application must also provide that the individual evaluation documentation requirements in 42 CFR 441.303(c) will be met, and the waiver must be limited to one or more permitted target groups, including aged or disabled individuals, individuals with intellectual or developmental disabilities, or individuals with mental illness.

In addition, the waiver request must include the person-centered planning process, including individual leadership of planning, informed choice, accessibility, conflict-resolution methods, and conflict-of-interest protections when an HCBS provider also provides case management or service-plan development.

Section 1915(c) itself [unverified: requires the state to give CMS satisfactory assurances that health and welfare safeguards and financial accountability are in place, that potentially eligible people will receive an evaluation of institutional level-of-care need, that they will be informed of feasible alternatives to institutional care, that the waiver will be cost-neutral on an average per-capita basis, and that the state will provide annual information to the Secretary on the waiver’s impact and recipients’ health and welfare].

North Carolina’s CAP/DA clinical policy says Medicaid covers CAP/DA when the beneficiary meets the required HCBS nursing facility level of care, needs long-term care support at a level typically provided in an institution, and has a documented medical diagnosis and functional care need.

The policy also requires a completed assessment showing a reasonable indication of need for at least one CAP/DA HCBS within 30 calendar days, a signed service plan authorizing one or more waiver services, the ability to maintain health, safety, and well-being in the home or approved location with formal and informal supports, and paid care needs that can be maintained within the average institutional cost of the CAP/DA waiver.

North Carolina also requires the beneficiary to have a primary physician who can link and coordinate medical services and to have an emergency back-up and disaster plan, which the policy calls a mandatory participation requirement.

The CAP/DA policy further states that Medicaid does not cover services under the policy when the beneficiary does not meet the eligibility requirements in Section 2.0 or the coverage criteria in Section 3.0, or when the service is duplicative, experimental, investigational, or part of a clinical trial.

North Carolina’s CAP/DA policy is currently reflected in the 2025-09-01 revision, and the change notice states that CMS approved the CAP/DA renewal waiver, with revisions aligned to the newly approved renewal effective 11/1/2024.

---

ID: sec:doc:federal_regulation:42-CFR-441:441.301
Title: Contents of request for a waiver
Section: 441.301
Policy: 42-CFR-441
Type: federal_regulation
Last revised: 2024-05-10
Federal Register cite: [46 FR 48541, Oct. 1, 1981, as amended at 50 FR 10026, Mar. 13, 1985; 59 FR 37717, July 25, 1994; 65 FR 60107, Oct. 10, 2000; 79 FR 3029, Jan. 16, 2014; 89 FR 40863, May 10, 2024]
Citation link: [42 CFR Part 441](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-441)
Reason: Primary federal waiver-authority or application-requirement section.
Content:
(a) A request for a waiver under this section must consist of the following:

(1) The assurances required by § 441.302 and the supporting documentation required by § 441.303.

(2) When applicable, requests for waivers of the requirements of section 1902(a)(1), section 1902(a)(10)(B), or section 1902(a)(10)(C)(i)(III) of the Act, which concern respectively, statewide application of Medicaid, comparability of services, and income and resource rules applicable to medically needy individuals living in the community.

(3) A statement explaining whether the agency will refuse to offer home or community-based services to any beneficiary if the agency can reasonably expect that the cost of the services would exceed the cost of an equivalent level of care provided in—

(i) A hospital (as defined in § 440.10 of this chapter);

(ii) A NF (as defined in section 1919(a) of the Act); or

(iii) An ICF/IID (as defined in § 440.150 of this chapter), if applicable.

(b) If the agency furnishes home and community-based services, as defined in § 440.180 of this subchapter, under a waiver granted under this subpart, the waiver request must—

(1) Provide that the services are furnished—

(i) Under a written person-centered service plan (also called plan of care) that is based on a person-centered approach and is subject to approval by the Medicaid agency.

(ii) Only to beneficiaries who are not inpatients of a hospital, NF, or ICF/IID; and

(iii) Only to beneficiaries who the agency determines would, in the absence of these services, require the Medicaid covered level of care provided in—

(A) A hospital (as defined in § 440.10 of this chapter);

(B) A NF (as defined in section 1919(a) of the Act); or

(C) An ICF/IID (as defined in § 440.150 of this chapter);

(2) Describe the qualifications of the individual or individuals who will be responsible for developing the individual plan of care;

(3) Describe the group or groups of individuals to whom the services will be offered;

(4) Describe the services to be furnished so that each service is separately defined. Multiple services that are generally considered to be separate services may not be consolidated under a single definition. Commonly accepted terms must be used to describe the service and definitions may not be open ended in scope. CMS will, however, allow combined service definitions (bundling) when this will permit more efficient delivery of services and not compromise either a beneficiary's access to or free choice of providers.

(5) Provide that the documentation requirements regarding individual evaluation, specified in § 441.303(c), will be met; and

(6) Be limited to one or more of the following target groups or any subgroup thereof that the State may define:

(i) Aged or disabled, or both.

(ii) Individuals with Intellectual or Developmental Disabilities, or both.

(iii) Mentally ill.

(c) A waiver request under this subpart must include the following—

(1) Person-centered planning process. The individual, or if applicable, the individual and the individual's authorized representative, will lead the person-centered planning process. When the term “individual” is used throughout § 441.301(c)(1) through (3), it includes the individual's authorized representative if applicable. In addition, the person-centered planning process:

(i) Includes people chosen by the individual.

(ii) Provides necessary information and support to ensure that the individual directs the process to the maximum extent possible, and is enabled to make informed choices and decisions.

(iii) Is timely and occurs at times and locations of convenience to the individual.

(iv) Reflects cultural considerations of the individual and is conducted by providing information in plain language and in a manner that is accessible to individuals with disabilities and persons who are limited English proficient, consistent with § 435.905(b) of this chapter.

(v) Includes strategies for solving conflict or disagreement within the process, including clear conflict-of-interest guidelines for all planning participants.

(vi) Providers of HCBS for the individual, or those who have an interest in or are employed by a provider of HCBS for the individual must not provide case management or develop the person-centered service plan, except when the State demonstrates that the only willing and qualified entity to provide case management and/or develop person-centered service plans in a geographic area also provides HCBS. In these cases, the State must devise conflict of interest protections including separation of entity and provider functions within provider entities, which must be approved by CMS. Individuals must be provided with a clear and accessible alternative dispute resolution process.

(vii) Offers informed choices to the individual regarding the services and supports they receive and from whom.

(viii) Includes a method for the individual to request updates to the plan as needed.

(ix) Records the alternative home and community-based settings that were considered by the individual.

(2) The Person-Centered Service Plan. The person-centered service plan must reflect the services and supports that are important for the individual to meet the needs identified through an assessment of functional need, as well as what is important to the individual with regard to preferences for the delivery of such services and supports. Commensurate with the level of need of the individual, and the scope of services and supports available under the State's 1915(c) HCBS waiver, the written plan must:

(i) Reflect that the setting in which the individual resides is chosen by the individual. The State must ensure that the setting chosen by the individual is integrated in, and supports full access of individuals receiving Medicaid HCBS to the greater community, including opportunities to seek employment and work in competitive integrated settings, engage in community life, control personal resources, and receive se

ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:3K-2:3.2.1
Title: 3.2.1 Specific criteria covered by Medicaid
Section: 3.2.1
Policy: 3K-2
Type: clinical_policy
Citation link: [Community Alternatives Program for Disabled Adults (CAP/DA)](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)
Reason: State implementation section from the NC policy document named by the question.
Content:
Medicaid shall cover CAP/DA when the beneficiary meets the following specific criteria:
Meets the required HCBS nursing facility LOC as determined by NC Medicaid and requires long-term care support at a level typically provided in an institution that is directly related to a documented medical diagnosis and functional care need, as assessed quarterly;
The completed CAP assessment finds there is a reasonable indication that the individual would need a service plan for at least one of the CAP/DA HCBS within 30 calendar days of the evaluation. Refer to Appendix F for reasonable indication of need ;
Have a signed service plan that authorizes one or more waiver services to be rendered on a monthly basis, that mitigates institutionalization through coordinated case management;
Have a signed service plan that authorizes an installation of equipment, modification or technology, on a short-term basis, to return to or remain in the primary private residence to prevent an institutional placement (the installation of equipment or modification must be completed within three calendar months of service plan approval);
Able to maintain health, safety and well-being at their primary private residence or an approved location with the use of both formal and informal supports, refer to Appendix F for definition of informal supports;
Paid care needs can be maintained within the average institutional cost of the CAP/DA waiver;
Has a primary physician that can link and coordinate all medical services;
Has an emergency back-up and disaster plan that specifies who shall provide care when key direct care staff cannot provide services or tasks as indicated in the current plan of care (POC), when the primary caregiver is experiencing an emergency, and when there is a public health emergency such as a weather event or pandemic.
Note: An emergency and disaster plan is a mandatory requirement that must be completed during the service plan development or within 30 calendar days of the initial and annual CAP/DA service plan approval. The emergency and disaster plan must be updated quarterly or during an emergency or pandemic.
Medicaid shall cover Consumer-Directed services when a beneficiary meets all of the above and the following criteria:
Understands the rights and responsibilities of directing their own care as evidenced by the completion of a mandatory self-assessment questionnaire and successful completion of an introductory consumer direction training and orientation Refer to Appendix C ;
Willing and emotionally capable to assume the responsibilities of an employer under the consumer-directed care by ensuring health and safety and identifying training opportunities to build competencies for him or herself and hired personal assistants as evidenced by a completed mandatory self-assessment questionnaire, or selects a representative who is willing and capable to assume the responsibilities to direct the beneficiary's care; and
Meets the specific criteria listed in Subsection 3.2.2(a) (b), and the following requirements:
Must have an approved service plan that identifies the amount, duration, frequency, and national provider identifier (NPI) of CAP/DA services and non-CAP/DA services as indicated in the beneficiary's service plan and approved by the Case Management Entity (CME);
Must have services provided according to all requirements specified in this policy; all applicable federal and state laws, rules, and regulations; the current standards of practice; and provider agency policies and procedures; and
Must sign and adhere to Beneficiary Rights and Responsibilities to indicate willingness to participate in CAP/DA.

the procedure, product, or service is individualized, specific, and consistent with symptoms or confirmed diagnosis of the illness or injury under treatment, and not in excess of the beneficiary's needs;
the procedure, product, or service can be safely furnished, and no equally effective and more conservative or less costly treatment is available statewide; and

Title: Section 1915(c). Waiver respecting medical assistance requirement in State plan; scope, etc.; "habilitation services" defined; imposition of certain regulatory limits prohibited; computation of expenditures for certain disabled patients; coordinated services; substitution of participants
Section: 1915(c)
Policy: SSA-Title-19
Type: federal_statute
Citation link: [Social Security Act — Title XIX (Medicaid)](https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-prelim-title42-chapter7-subchapter19)

Content:
(c) Waiver respecting medical assistance requirement in State plan; scope, etc.; "habilitation services" defined; imposition of certain regulatory limits prohibited; computation of expenditures for certain disabled patients; coordinated services; substitution of participants

(1) The Secretary may by waiver provide that a State plan approved under this subchapter may include as "medical assistance" under such plan payment for part or all of the cost of home or community-based services (other than room and board) approved by the Secretary which are provided pursuant to a written plan of care to individuals with respect to whom there has been a determination that but for the provision of such services the individuals would require the level of care provided in a hospital or a nursing facility or intermediate care facility for the mentally retarded the cost of which could be reimbursed under the State plan. For purposes of this subsection, the term "room and board" shall not include an amount established under a method determined by the State to reflect the portion of costs of rent and food attributable to an unrelated personal caregiver who is residing in the same household with an individual who, but for the assistance of such caregiver, would require admission to a hospital, nursing facility, or intermediate care facility for the mentally retarded.

(2) A waiver shall not be granted under this subsection unless the State provides assurances satisfactory to the Secretary that—

(A) necessary safeguards (including adequate standards for provider participation) have been taken to protect the health and welfare of individuals provided services under the waiver and to assure financial accountability for funds expended with respect to such services;

(B) the State will provide, with respect to individuals who—

(i) are entitled to medical assistance for inpatient hospital services, nursing facility services, or services in an intermediate care facility for the mentally retarded under the State plan,

(ii) may require such services, and

(iii) may be eligible for such home or community-based care under such waiver,

for an evaluation of the need for inpatient hospital services, nursing facility services, or services in an intermediate care facility for the mentally retarded;

(C) such individuals who are determined to be likely to require the level of care provided in a hospital, nursing facility, or intermediate care facility for the mentally retarded are informed of the feasible alternatives, if available under the waiver, at the choice of such individuals, to the provision of inpatient hospital services, nursing facility services, or services in an intermediate care facility for the mentally retarded;

(D) under such waiver the average per capita expenditure estimated by the State in any fiscal year for medical assistance provided with respect to such individuals does not exceed 100 percent of the average per capita expenditure that the State reasonably estimates would have been made in that fiscal year for expenditures under the State plan for such individuals if the waiver had not been granted; and

(E) the State will provide to the Secretary annually, consistent with a data collection plan designed by the Secretary, information on the impact of the waiver granted under this subsection on the type and amount of medical assistance provided under the State plan and on the health and welfare of recipients.

(3) A waiver granted under this subsection may include a waiver of the requirements of section 1396a(a)(1) of this title (relating to statewideness), section 1396a(a)(10)(B) of this title (relating to comparability), and section 1396a(a)(10)(C)(i)(III) of this title (relating to income and resource rules applicable in the community). A waiver under this subsection (other than a waiver described in paragraph (11) or subsection (h)(2)) shall be for an initial term of three years and, upon the request of a State, shall be extended for additional five-year periods unless the Secretary determines that for the previous waiver period the assurances provided under paragraph (2) have not been met. A waiver may provide, with respect to post-eligibility treatment of income of all individuals receiving services under that waiver, that the maximum amount of the individual's income which may be disregarded for any month for the maintenance needs of the individual may be an amount greater than the maximum allowed for that purpose under regulations in effect on July 1, 1985.

(4) A waiver granted under this subsection may, consistent with paragraph (2)—

(A) limit the individuals provided benefits under such waiver to individuals with respect to whom the State has determined that there is a reasonable expectation that the amount of medical assistance provided with respect to the individual under such waiver will not exceed the amount of such medical assistance provided for such individual if the waiver did not apply, and

(B) provide medical assistance to individuals (to the extent consistent with written plans of care, which are subject to the approval of the State) for case management services, homemaker/home health aide services and personal care services, adult day health services, habilitation services, respite care, and such other services requested by the State as the Secretary may approve and for day treatment or other partial hospitalization services, psychosocial rehabilitation services, and clinic services (whether or not furnished in a facility) for individuals with chronic mental illness.

Except as provided under paragraph (2)(D), the Secretary may not restrict the number of hours or days of respite care in any period which a State may provide under a waiver under this subsection.
