ID: sec:doc:federal_regulation:42-CFR-431:431.205
Title: Provision of hearing system
Section: 431.205
Policy: 42-CFR-431
Type: federal_regulation
Last revised: 2016-11-30
Federal Register cite: [44 FR 17932, Mar. 29, 1979, as amended at 78 FR 42301, July 15, 2013; 81 FR 86448, Nov. 30, 2016]
Citation link: [42 CFR Part 431](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-431)

Content:
(a) The Medicaid agency must be responsible for maintaining a hearing system that meets the requirements of this subpart.

(b) The State's hearing system must provide for—

(1) A hearing before—

(i) The Medicaid agency; or

(ii) For the denial of eligibility for individuals whose income eligibility is determined based on the applicable modified adjusted gross income standard described in§ 435.911(c) of this chapter, the Exchange or Exchange appeals entity to which authority to conduct fair hearings has been delegated under § 431.10(c)(1)(ii), provided that individuals who have requested a fair hearing are given the choice to have their fair hearing conducted instead by the Medicaid agency; at state option the Exchange or Exchange appeals entity decision may be subject to review by the Medicaid agency in accordance with § 431.10(c)(3)(iii); or

(2) An evidentiary hearing at the local level, with a right of appeal to the Medicaid agency.

(c) The agency may offer local hearings in some political subdivisions and not in others.

(d) The hearing system must meet the due process standards set forth in Goldberg v. Kelly, 397 U.S. 254 (1970), and any additional standards specified in this subpart.

(e) The hearing system must be accessible to persons who are limited English proficient and persons who have disabilities, consistent with § 435.905(b) of this chapter.

(f) The hearing system must comply with the United States Constitution, the Social Security Act, title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990, the Age Discrimination Act of 1975, and section 1557 of the Affordable Care Act and implementing regulations.

[Authority: [44 FR 17932, Mar. 29, 1979, as amended at 78 FR 42301, July 15, 2013; 81 FR 86448, Nov. 30, 2016]]

[getSection]
ID: sec:doc:federal_regulation:42-CFR-431:431.206
Title: Informing applicants and beneficiaries
Section: 431.206
Policy: 42-CFR-431
Type: federal_regulation
Last revised: 2016-11-30
Federal Register cite: [44 FR 17932, Mar. 29, 1979, as amended at 57 FR 56505, Nov. 30, 1992; 58 FR 25784, Apr. 28, 1993; 78 FR 42301, July 15, 2013; 81 FR 68847, Oct. 4, 2016; 81 FR 86448, Nov. 30, 2016]
Citation link: [42 CFR Part 431](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-431)

Content:
(a) The agency must issue and publicize its hearing procedures.

(b) The agency must, at the time specified in paragraph (c) of this section, inform every applicant or beneficiary in writing—

(1) Of his or her right to a fair hearing and right to request an expedited fair hearing;

(2) Of the method by which he may obtain a hearing;

(3) That he may represent himself or use legal counsel, a relative, a friend, or other spokesman; and

(4) Of the time frames in which the agency must take final administrative action, in accordance with § 431.244(f).

(c) The agency must provide the information required in paragraph (b) of this section—(1) At the time that the individual applies for Medicaid;

(2) At the time the agency denies an individual's claim for eligibility, benefits or services; or denies a request for exemption from mandatory enrollment in an Alternative Benefit Plan; or takes other action, as defined at § 431.201; or whenever a hearing is otherwise required in accordance with § 431.220(a);

(3) At the time a skilled nursing facility or a nursing facility notifies a resident in accordance with § 483.15 of this chapter that he or she is to be transferred or discharged; and

(4) At the time an individual receives an adverse determination by the State with regard to the preadmission screening and annual resident review requirements of section 1919(e)(7) of the Act.

(d) If, in accordance with § 431.10(c)(1)(ii), the agency has delegated authority to the Exchange or Exchange appeals entity to conduct the fair hearing, the agency must inform the individual in writing that—

(1) He or she has the right to have his or her hearing before the agency, instead of the Exchange or the Exchange appeals entity; and

(2) The method by which the individual may make such election;

(e) The information required under this subpart must be accessible to individuals who are limited English proficient and to individuals with disabilities, consistent with § 435.905(b) of this chapter, and may be provided in electronic format in accordance with § 435.918 of this chapter.

ID: sec:doc:dhhs_policy:MA-3430:url-e7293cdc89d4:_s48
Title: 2. State Hearing
Policy: MA-3430
Type: dhhs_policy
Citation link: [MA-3430 NOTICE AND HEARINGS PROCESS](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/ma-3430-4.pdf)

Content:
A State Hearing Officer from the DHHS Hearings and Appeals Section presides at the hearing and administers the oath or affirmation to all participants.
The State Hearing Officer will also record the hearing.  A transcript will not be prepared unless a petition to Superior Court is filed.
The a/b and the local agency may be represented by attorneys or other individuals obtained at their expense.
The local agency and the a/b must each designate someone to present their testimony and to call as witnesses.  Any person testifying must be sworn in.
The local agency representative must read the summary and explain the county's action or call upon someone to do so.  They may call witnesses, one at a time.  The State Hearing Officer may question witnesses during their testimony.  When the county's testimony has ended, the a/b or their representative may question the county's witnesses or representative.
The a/b or their designated authorized representative may then explain why they feel the local agency's action should not be implemented.  They may call witnesses, one at a time.  The State Hearing Officer may question witnesses during testimony.  When the a/b's testimony has ended, the local agency representative may question the a/b, witnesses, or representative.
Representatives for the local agency and the a/b may present closing statements summarizing their view of the situation in question.

[getSection]
ID: sec:doc:dhhs_policy:MA-3430:url-e7293cdc89d4:_s51
Title: 2. State Hearing
Policy: MA-3430
Type: dhhs_policy
Citation link: [MA-3430 NOTICE AND HEARINGS PROCESS](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/ma-3430-4.pdf)

Content:
The State Hearing Officer must render a decision on the case, based on appropriate regulations and evidence presented at the hearing.  Those factors must be cited in a written statement of decision:

| 0                  | 1                                                                                                                               |
|:-------------------|:--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Standard Hearing:  | • Not more than 90 calendar days from the date of the state appeal request unless the hearing was delayed at the a/b's request. |
| Expedited Hearing: | • Not more than 7 working days from the date of the state appeal request unless the hearing was delayed at the a/b's request.   |

If the hearing is delayed at the a/b's request, the hearing decision can only be delayed for the length of time allowed for the a/b's delay.
If a state hearing has been held and the county has not received a response the worker needs to contact DHHS Hearings and Appeals Section to check the status of the decision:

| 0                  | 1                                                                                                                         |
|:-------------------|:--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Standard Hearing:  | • After 14 calendar days, the worker needs to contact DHHSHearings and Appeals to check the status of the decision.       |
| Expedited Hearing: | • After five (5) working days, the worker needs to contact DHHS Hearings and Appeals to check the status of the decision. |

The hearing officer will prepare a tentative decision, which will be sent by mail to the a/b, the local agency and representatives. Decisions reversing the local agency's action are sent by certified mail to the local agency. Decisions affirming the local agency's action are sent certified mail to the a/b. Decisions are sent by regular mail to representatives. The tentative hearing decision becomes a final decision 10 calendar days from the date of the Notice of Decision if the tentative decision is not contested.
The local agency or the a/b may contest a tentative hearing decision by presenting oral and/or written arguments, for or against the Notice of Decision, no later than 10 calendar days from the date of the Notice of Decision.  Both must contact the Chief Hearing Officer to present arguments.  No new evidence will be accepted at this level of the appeal process.
If no written argument, a request for a time extension to submit a written argument, or a request for oral argument is made within 10 calendar days of the date of the tentative decision, the tentative hearing decision becomes final.
If the party that requested oral argument fails to appear for the scheduled oral argument, or the party failed to timely submit a written argument, the tentative decision becomes final.
If contested timely, then a Final Decision is issued by a designated official of the Hearings & Appeals Section and sent by certified mail to both the a/b and the local agency.  The Final Decision is sent by regular mail to representatives.

per_question.question: Will the adult dental benefit in NC Medicaid pay for cosmetic teeth whitening?
per_question.agent_answer:

[Policy 4A § 4.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/4a-dental-services/download?attachment) The current authoritative document I checked is Dental Services, effective December 15, 2023. [Policy 4A § 1.0](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/4a-dental-services/download?attachment)

If you want, I can also check whether there is any different rule for beneficiaries under age 21 through EPSDT.

ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:4A:_s148
Title: A.22 Billing for Services Covered by Medicare and Medicaid
Policy: 4A
Type: clinical_policy
Citation link: [Dental Services](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/4a-dental-services/download?attachment)
Reason: Matched not covered.
Content:
Federal law mandates that Medicaid be the payer of last resort when beneficiaries are covered by both Medicare and Medicaid. According to the Medicare Benefit Policy Manual published by CMS, Medicare does not cover 'services in connection with the care, treatment, filling, removal or replacement of teeth or structures directly supporting the teeth…. 'Structures directly supporting the teeth' means periodontium, which includes the gingivae, dentogingival junction, periodontal membrane, cementum of the teeth, and alveolar process.'
Medicare Part B does cover certain oral surgical services performed by dentists or oral surgeons as long as they are not provided primarily for the care, treatment, filling, removal, or replacement of teeth or structures directly supporting the teeth. Examples of Medicare-covered services include extractions in preparation for radiation therapy, reduction of jaw fractures, and removal of tumors of the jaw.
Services that are not covered by Medicare but are covered by Medicaid shall be filed directly with Medicaid on the 2019 ADA Dental Claim Form. Services covered by Medicare and performed either in the emergency room or in the office must first be filed with the Medicare Part B carrier using the CMS-1500 claim form.
Note: For dually eligible Medicare and Medicaid beneficiaries, dental services covered by Medicare do not require Medicaid prior approval.
The dental services listed below must be filed first with the beneficiary's Medicare Part B carrier on a CMS-1500 claim form. Typically, it is necessary to file such Medicare claims using Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) codes, published by the American Medical Association; therefore, convert the CDT codes shown here to CPT codes.

| 0     | 1     | 2     | 3     | 4     |
|:------|:------|:------|:------|:------|
| D7285 | D7465 | D7740 | D7872 | D7948 |
| D7286 | D7490 | D7750 | D7873 | D7949 |
| D7288 | D7540 | D7760 | D7910 | D7950 |
| D7410 | D7610 | D7780 | D7911 | D7955 |
| D7411 | D7620 | D7810 | D7912 | D7979 |
| D7412 | D7630 | D7820 | D7920 | D7980 |
| D7413 | D7640 | D7830 | D7940 | D7981 |
| D7414 | D7650 | D7840 | D7941 | D7982 |
| D7415 | D7660 | D7850 | D7943 | D7983 |
| D7440 | D7680 | D7858 | D7944 | D7990 |
| D7441 | D7710 | D7860 | D7945 | D7991 |
| D7460 | D7720 | D7865 | D7946 |       |
| D7461 | D7730 | D7870 | D7947 |       |

Professional claims filed to Medicare as the primary payer should be crossed over automatically to Medicaid. In order for the crossover claim to process, the NPI on the Medicare claim must be on file for a North Carolina Medicaid Provider Number (MPN). It is the provider's responsibility to check the Medicaid Remittance and Status Report to verify that the claim was crossed over from Medicare.
Claims that do not crossover and have been paid by Medicare can be filed as an 837 professional transaction by completing the Coordination of Benefits (COB) loop. Refer to the implementation guide at http://wpc-edi.com and the NC Medicaid HIPAA Companion Guide on NC Medicaid's website at https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/draft-daily-weekly-eb-monthly-834o-companion-guide20190605-v2-0/open for instructions on completing the 837 professional transaction.
Claims that do not cross over, have been paid by Medicare, and are included on the electronic submission exceptions list at https://www.nctracks.nc.gov/content/public/providers/claims.html can be filed on a CMS-1500 claim form. The paper claim form must be submitted with the Medicare voucher attached. If claims do not cross over, have been paid by Medicare, and are not included on the electronic submission exceptions list, the claims must be submitted electronically.
When the procedure(s) is denied by Medicare, the provider shall submit the comparable 2023 CDT code(s) directly to Medicaid on a paper 2019 ADA Dental Claim Form with the Medicare voucher and Medicaid Resolution Inquiry form attached. This will allow the claim to process appropriately according to NC Medicaid policy.

per_question.question: Under the respiratory equipment policy (5A-2), can an adult beneficiary get a brand-new replacement CPAP machine every year?
per_question.agent_answer:
No. An adult cannot automatically get a brand-new replacement CPAP machine every year under Policy 5A-2. The policy ties replacement to the item’s established lifetime expectancy in Attachment A, Section C, and it says replacement may be considered when repair is no longer cost-effective and the item is out of warranty. If replacement is requested before the usual life expectancy ends, the provider must explain on the CMN/PA form why early replacement is needed.

The policy also says Medicaid may place limits based on medical necessity, and if the prescriber orders equipment beyond quantity limits or lifetime expectancy, the DME provider must seek prior approval for an override through NCTracks with additional medical-necessity documentation.

For purchased equipment, the policy expects service and repairs to be handled under warranty first, and if there is no warranty, repair can be requested with prior approval; Medicaid does not cover maintenance or service contracts.

So the practical answer is: an adult does not have a yearly entitlement to a new CPAP machine, but an earlier replacement might be approved if there is documented medical necessity or another policy-supported reason for replacement before the usual lifetime expectancy.

This is based on the current April 1, 2025 version of Policy 5A-2, which was amended throughout for clarity and consistency.

If you want, I can next try to pin down the exact CPAP-machine lifetime expectancy row from Attachment A, Section C.

---

*Suggested citations for uncited claims above:*
- [Policy 5A-2 § 5.9](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/5a-2-respiratory-equipment-and-supplies/download?attachment)
- [Policy 5A-2 § 5.5](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/5a-2-respiratory-equipment-and-supplies/download?attachment)
- [Policy 5A-2 § 5.8](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/5a-2-respiratory-equipment-and-supplies/download?attachment)
- [Policy 5A-2 Change Notice 2025-04-01](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/5a-2-respiratory-equipment-and-supplies/download?attachment)

However, the agent misses the reference answer's specific mention of section 3.2.1 coverage criteria and section 4.2.1 non-coverage criteria as the primary policy hooks for frequency limits. uncited_claims: An adult cannot automatically get a brand-new replacement CPAP machine every year under Policy 5A-2.

The policy ties replacement to the item’s established lifetime expectancy in Attachment A, Section C, and it says replacement may be considered when repair is no longer cost-effective and the item is out of warranty.

The policy also says Medicaid may place limits based on medical necessity, and if the prescriber orders equipment beyond quantity limits or lifetime expectancy, the DME provider must seek prior approval for an override through NCTracks with additional medical-necessity documentation.

For purchased equipment, the policy expects service and repairs to be handled under warranty first, and if there is no warranty, repair can be requested with prior approval; Medicaid does not cover maintenance or service contracts.
This is based on the current April 1, 2025 version of Policy 5A-2, which was amended throughout for clarity and consistency.

ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:5A-2:_s46
Title: Requirements for Coverage
Policy: 5A-2
Type: clinical_policy
Citation link: [Respiratory Equipment and Supplies](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/5a-2-respiratory-equipment-and-supplies/download?attachment)
Reason: Matched cover.
Content:
A polysomnogram must be submitted with the initial request for a RAD with those diagnoses that have a polysomnogram requirement in the criteria.
Medicaid shall not accept polysomnograms that are performed by a medical equipment provider . Polysomnograms must be provided according to requirements listed in Clinical Coverage Policy 1A-20, Sleep Studies and Polysomnography Services , on Medicaid's website: https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/.
The polysomnogram must be based on a minimum of two (2) hours of recorded sleep time without the use of a CPAP or RAD device, reported by the polysomnogram. The polysomnogram must include sleep staging and other sleep parameters such as airflow, respiratory effort, and oxygen saturation by oximetry.
If the polysomnogram criteria listed above are not met, claims submitted for reimbursement of a RAD and related accessories are denied as not medically necessary.
For an item to be covered by Medicaid a written signed and dated order from the 'treating physician' must be received by the supplier before the CMN/PA form is submitted for prior approval. The treating physician is one who is qualified by virtue of experience and training in non-invasive respiratory assistance, to order and monitor the use of the respiratory assist devices.
If there is a discontinuation of the RAD at any time, the provider is expected to determine that the RAD has been discontinued and stop billing for the equipment and related accessories.
A RAD with a back-up rate is not medically necessary if the primary diagnosis is OSA.
Initial Prior Approval: For a RAD to be covered, the treating physician, physician assistant, or nurse practitioner, shall fully document in the beneficiary's clinical health record those symptoms characteristic of sleepassociated hypoventilation, such as daytime hypersomnolence, excessive fatigue, morning headache, cognitive dysfunction, or dyspnea, etc.
Initial prior approval for a RAD is given for a period of six (6) months .
Note: A RAD without a back-up rate is reimbursed as a rental only and not to exceed a total of monthly rental payments equal to the purchase price. A RAD with a back-up rate is reimbursed as a continuous rental item.
Renewal Prior Approval: For renewal prior approval and continued coverage of the RAD beyond the first six (6) months of therapy, no sooner than the fifth (5 th ) month after initiating therapy:
The provider shall obtain a statement of compliance from the treating physician declaring that the beneficiary is using the device an average of four (4) hours per 24-hour period this must be submitted along with the CMN/PA form request for renewal. Failure of the beneficiary to be consistently using the RAD for an average of four (4) hours per the 24-hour period by the time of the reevaluation would represent non-compliant use and constitute reason for Medicaid to deny continued coverage as not medically necessary; and
A statement must be submitted by the physician, physician assistant, or nurse practitioner indicating the progress of relevant symptoms and that the RAD is still medically necessary.
Note: A non-heated or heated humidifier is covered by Medicaid with the use of a RAD. The treating physician shall specify which type of humidifier the beneficiary is to use.

ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:5A-2:Attachment D
Title: Attachment D: Requesting Unlisted DME and Supplies for Adults
Section: Attachment D
Policy: 5A-2
Type: clinical_policy
Citation link: [Respiratory Equipment and Supplies](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/5a-2-respiratory-equipment-and-supplies/download?attachment)
Reason: Matched cover.
Content:
In compliance with the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) Home Health Final Rule, 42 CFR Part 440.70, please follow these guidelines when requesting medical necessity reviews for DME and supplies for adults not listed in Attachment A, Section C or the DME fee schedule.
a . The general requirements and criteria set forth in clinical coverage policy 5A-2 must be met.
This includes, but is not limited to:
The item being requested must fit the definition of durable medical equipment or supplies;
The beneficiary must be enrolled in the Medicaid program and be eligible for the item;
The provider must be enrolled in the Medicaid program with an appropriate taxonomy;
The requested item must be safe, effective, economical and not intended for the convenience of the beneficiary, the beneficiary's caregiver, or the provider;
The item must be medical in nature, generally recognized as an accepted method of treatment, and must not be experimental or investigational;
The item must be ordered by a physician, physician assistant, or nurse practitioner; and
The item must be medically necessary to maintain or improve a beneficiary's medical, physical or functional level, and appropriate for use in any non-institutional setting in which normal life activities take place;
A documented face-to-face encounter with the beneficiary and the ordering physician, physician assistant, or nurse practitioner related to the primary reason the beneficiary requires the item must have occurred no more than six months prior to the initiation of durable medical equipment or supplies; and
The beneficiary's need for the item must be reviewed by the ordering physician, physician assistant, or nurse practitioner at least annually.
If the provider determines that the applicable requirements and criteria set forth in clinical coverage policy 5A-2 have been met, then the provider may submit a completed Certificate of Medical Necessity/Prior Approval (CMN/PA form) and the usual supportive prior approval documentation, through NCTracks for a medical necessity review.
Providers may request non-covered, unlisted, or restricted items using their identifiable HCPCS code (such as E1012). If no HCPCS code exists, providers may use the miscellaneous combination K0108/W4005 for wheelchair accessories only, and for non-wheelchair items, the miscellaneous combination E1399/W4047.
Items approved by this procedure may be manually priced. Please include the appropriate manual pricing documentation with the prior approval request (see May 2017 Medicaid Bulletin for details).
Providers should expect medical necessity reviews using this procedure to take longer than usual.
Claims for items approved using this procedure should also be submitted through NCTracks.
If denied, the provider and beneficiary will be notified, and normal beneficiary appeal rights will apply.
Providers will be notified if the device requested is covered by a different Medicaid policy area or waiver program.

ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:5A-2:5.8
Title: 5.8 Servicing and Repairing Medical Equipment
Section: 5.8
Policy: 5A-2
Type: clinical_policy
Citation link: [Respiratory Equipment and Supplies](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/5a-2-respiratory-equipment-and-supplies/download?attachment)
Reason: Matched not covered.
Content:
Service and repair of medical equipment is handled in one of three ways:
Rental Equipment: Service and repairs are provided as part of the rental arrangement with no additional charge to Medicaid.
Purchased Equipment Warranty: Service and repairs are handled under any warranty coverage an item may have. If there is no warranty, providers may request prior approval to perform the needed service and repairs by submitting a completed CMN/PA form with a repair estimate to NCTracks. The estimate must show a breakdown of charges for parts and the number of hours of labor. No charge is allowed for pick-up or delivery of the item or for the assembly of Medicaid reimbursed parts.
Purchased Equipment Non-Warranty: Service or repair is covered if the equipment is owned by the beneficiary and if the repair is not covered under the warranty. A repair estimate must be provided. The estimate must show a breakdown of charges for parts and the number of hours of labor. No charge is allowed for pick-up or delivery, for the assembly of Medicaid reimbursed parts or for freight or the provider's travel time or expenses. All the following information must be documented in block 30 of the CMN/PA form:
The description and HCPCS code of the item being serviced or repaired.
The age of the item.
The number of times the item has been previously repaired.
The current replacement cost.
Note: Providers shall have emergency repair service available 24-hours a day, seven days a week for any life-sustaining equipment they provide.
Note: Medicaid shall not cover maintenance or service contracts.

ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:5A-2:5.3.6
Title: 5.3.6 Miscellaneous Durable Medical Equipment and Supplies
Section: 5.3.6
Policy: 5A-2
Type: clinical_policy
Citation link: [Respiratory Equipment and Supplies](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/5a-2-respiratory-equipment-and-supplies/download?attachment)
Reason: Matched limitation.
Content:
Refer to Attachment A, Section C: Procedure Code(s) for a list of HCPCS codes, established lifetime expectancies and quantity limitations for Durable Medical Equipment and Supplies. To request a medical necessity review for an item not listed, refer to sections 1.2 , 2.2 and Attachment D for instructions.
A manual ventilation bag requires prior approval and is covered when a beneficiary has a life-threatening diagnosis and requires ventilator support.
Peak flow meters are covered when a beneficiary's physician deems it medically necessary for the beneficiary to monitor his peak expiratory flow rate on a regular basis.
Supplies for use with metered dose inhalers are covered when ordered by the physician who has also ordered a medically necessary metered dose inhaler for the beneficiary.
A respiratory suction pump, catheters, canisters, and tubing are covered if a beneficiary is physically unable to independently expectorate respiratory secretions.
For prior approval requirements refer to the Durable Medical Equipment and Supply fee schedule on Medicaid's website at: https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/. Items that require prior approval are identified on the Durable Medical Equipment Fee Schedule .

Title: 5.3.1 Oxygen, Oxygen Supplies, and Equipment
Section: 5.3.1
Policy: 5A-2
Type: clinical_policy
Citation link: [Respiratory Equipment and Supplies](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/5a-2-respiratory-equipment-and-supplies/download?attachment)

Content:
Refer to Attachment A, Section C: Procedure Code(s) for a list of HCPCS codes, established lifetime expectancies and quantity limitations for Durable Medical Equipment and Supplies. To request a medical necessity review for an item not listed, refer to sections 1.2 , 2.2 and Attachment D for instructions.
Medicaid shall cover oxygen therapy and related supplies and equipment for a beneficiary who meets the following criteria:
Ages zero (0) through three (3) years : arterial oxyhemoglobin saturation (SaO2) equal to or less than 94% and have a documented supporting diagnosis.
Ages 4 through 20 years: SaO2 equal to or less than 90% and a documented supporting diagnosis.
Ages 21 and older: there is documentation from the treating physician that reports ALL of the following:
A diagnosis of severe lung disease or hypoxia-related symptoms that might be expected to improve with oxygen therapy,
Alternative treatments have been tried and considered or deemed clinically ineffective,

Title: f. Individually Priced Items:
Policy: 5A-2
Type: clinical_policy
Citation link: [Respiratory Equipment and Supplies](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/5a-2-respiratory-equipment-and-supplies/download?attachment)
Reason: Matched limitation.
Content:
These items are reviewed on an individual basis and manually priced.
Refer to Attachment A, Section C: Procedure Code(s) for a list of HCPCS codes, established lifetime expectancies and quantity limitations for Durable Medical Equipment and Supplies.
For the rates associated with the list of equipment, supplies, and services found in Attachment A, Section C, refer to the Durable Medical Equipment fee schedule at https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/.
In compliance with the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) Home Health Final Rule Title 42, §440.70, items not listed in Attachment A, Section C or in the Durable Medical Equipment fee schedule will be considered for coverage if requested by a provider, or a beneficiary through a provider, and submitted for prior approval review of medical necessity. For beneficiaries under age 21, please request an 'EPSDT review' using NCTracks. Refer to section 2.2 Special Provisions for more information about EPSDT. For beneficiaries aged 21 and older, please submit the request through NCTracks per the procedure detailed in Attachment D .
Note: As a subcategory of Durable Medical Equipment and Supplies, the terms Respiratory Equipment and Supplies, Medical Equipment and Supplies, and Durable Medical Equipment and Supplies are used interchangeably throughout this policy.

ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:5A-2:5.5
Title: 5.5 Durable Medical Equipment and Supplies Limitations
Section: 5.5
Policy: 5A-2
Type: clinical_policy
Effective: 2025-04-01
Citation link: [Respiratory Equipment and Supplies](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/5a-2-respiratory-equipment-and-supplies/download?attachment)

Content:
Medicaid may place appropriate limits, based on medical necessity criteria, on Durable Medical Equipment and Supplies. When the prescribing physician, physician assistant, or nurse practitioner, orders equipment or supplies beyond these limits, the DME provider shall seek prior approval for these items through NCTracks.
A PA request for an override of a quantity limit, or lifetime expectancy must include the usual PA documentation ( Subsections 5.2 and 5.3 ) along with the following additional information:
The item being requested for an override clearly marked on the CMN/PA form.
The type of override (quantity limit, or lifetime expectancy) clearly stated.
An explanation of the medical necessity for the override from the physician, physician assistant, nurse practitioner, or therapist.
Override PA requests are reviewed for medical necessity as per usual PA review timelines. Override PA review outcomes are communicated to providers and beneficiaries in the same way as a typical PA request.
Refer to Attachment A, Section C: Procedure Code(s) for a listing of the established lifetime expectancies and quantity limitations for Durable Medical Equipment and Supplies. To request a medical necessity review for an item not listed, refer to sections 1.2 , 2.2 and Attachment D for instructions.

Title: 5.9 Replacing Medical Equipment

Effective: 2025-04-01
Citation link: [Respiratory Equipment and Supplies](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/5a-2-respiratory-equipment-and-supplies/download?attachment)

Content:
Medicaid may consider replacing the item, when repairing is no longer cost-effective and the item is out of warranty, Refer to Attachment A, Section C: Procedure Codes(s). To request a medical necessity review for an item not listed, see sections 1.2 , 2.2 and Attachment D for instructions.
Note: When requesting prior approval for the replacement of an item before its usual life expectancy has ended, explain on the CMN/PA form why the replacement is needed.
Specific documentation, in addition to the prescription and CMN/PA form, is required in the following situations:
In cases of equipment loss or damage beyond repair, a letter from the social worker, case manager or child service coordinator explaining the circumstances.
In cases of theft, a copy of the police report or a letter from the appropriate person with knowledge of the occurrence, such as the school principal, social worker, etc.
In cases of equipment destruction by fire, a copy of the fire report.
In cases of wide-spread natural disasters, documentation is accepted from any of the entities listed above or from the NC Division of Emergency Management, Federal Emergency Management Agency, American Red Cross, the National Guard or other appropriate state or local authorities and agencies on the ground in the affected areas.

ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:5A-2:2.2.1
Title: 2.2.1 EPSDT Special Provision: Exception to Policy Limitations for a Medicaid Beneficiary under 21 Years of Age
Section: 2.2.1
Policy: 5A-2
Type: clinical_policy
Effective: 2025-04-01
Citation link: [Respiratory Equipment and Supplies](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/5a-2-respiratory-equipment-and-supplies/download?attachment)

Content:
42 U.S.C. § 1396d(r) [1905(r) of the Social Security Act]
Early and Periodic Screening, Diagnostic, and Treatment (EPSDT) is a federal Medicaid requirement that requires the state Medicaid agency to cover services, products, or procedures for Medicaid beneficiary under 21 years of age if the service is medically necessary health care to correct or ameliorate a defect, physical or mental illness, or a condition [health problem] identified through a screening examination (includes any evaluation by a physician or other licensed practitioner).
This means EPSDT covers most of the medical or remedial care a child needs to improve or maintain his or her health in the best condition possible, compensate for a health problem, prevent it from worsening, or prevent the development of additional health problems.
Medically necessary services will be provided in the most economic mode, as long as the treatment made available is similarly efficacious to the service requested by the beneficiary's physician, therapist, or other licensed practitioner; the determination process does not delay the delivery of the needed service; and the determination does not limit the beneficiary's right to a free choice of providers.
EPSDT does not require the state Medicaid agency to provide any service, product or procedure:
that is unsafe, ineffective, or experimental or investigational.
that is not medical in nature or not generally recognized as an accepted method of medical practice or treatment.
Amended Date: April 1, 2025
Service limitations on scope, amount, duration, frequency, location of service, and other specific criteria described in clinical coverage policies may be exceeded or may not apply as long as the provider's documentation shows that the requested service is medically necessary 'to correct or ameliorate a defect, physical or mental illness, or a condition' [health problem]; that is, provider documentation shows how the service, product, or procedure meets all EPSDT criteria, including to correct or improve or maintain the beneficiary's health in the best condition possible, compensate for a health problem, prevent it from worsening, or prevent the development of additional health problems.

[getSection]
ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:5A-2:5.3.2
Title: 5.3.2 Respiratory Devices for the Treatment of Respiratory Disorders other than Obstructive Sleep Apnea (OSA)
Section: 5.3.2
Policy: 5A-2
Type: clinical_policy
Effective: 2025-04-01
Citation link: [Respiratory Equipment and Supplies](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/5a-2-respiratory-equipment-and-supplies/download?attachment)

Content:
Refer to Attachment A, Section C : Procedure Code(s) for a list of HCPCS codes, established lifetime expectancies and quantity limitations for Durable Medical Equipment and Supplies. To request a medical necessity review for an item not listed, see sections 1.2, 2.2 and Attachment D for instructions.
A respiratory assist device (RAD) BiLevel without back-up rate delivers adjustable, variable levels (within a single respiratory cycle) of positive air pressure by way of tubing and a noninvasive interface to assist spontaneous respiratory efforts and supplement the volume of inspired air into the lungs (such as, noninvasive positive pressure respiratory assistance: NIPPRA).
A RAD BiLevel with back-up rate delivers adjustable, variable levels (within a single respiratory cycle) of positive air pressure by way of tubing and a noninvasive interface to assist spontaneous respiratory efforts and supplement the volume of inspired air into the lungs. In addition, it has a timed back-up feature to deliver this air pressure whenever sufficient spontaneous inspiratory efforts fail to occur.
Medicaid shall cover RADs and related accessories for beneficiaries with ANY of the following respiratory disorders who demonstrate medical necessity for each disorder:
Restrictive thoracic disorders:
The beneficiary shall meet any one of the following criteria:
Documentation of the beneficiary's progressive neuromuscular disease or severe thoracic cage abnormality and an arterial blood gas PaCO2, done while awake and breathing the beneficiary's usual fraction of inspired oxygen (FIO2), that is greater than or equal to 45 mmHg;
Sleep oximetry demonstrating oxygen saturation less than or equal to 88 percent for at least five (5) continuous minutes, done while breathing the beneficiary's FIO2; or
For a progressive neuromuscular disease (only), maximal inspiratory pressure is less than 60cm H20 or forced vital capacity is less than 50% predicted; and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease does not contribute significantly to the beneficiary's pulmonary limitation.
Severe chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD):
The beneficiary must meet the following criteria:
Documentation of the beneficiary's severe COPD and an arterial blood gas study, done while awake and breathing the beneficiary's usual FIO2, demonstrating a PaCO2 that is greater than or equal to 52 mmHg; and one of the following:
Sleep oximetry demonstrating oxygen saturation less than or equal to 88 percent for at least five (5) minutes in total, done while breathing the beneficiary's usual FIO2; or
Prior to initiating therapy, OSA (treatment with CPAP) has been considered and ruled out.
Prior Approval is required for a RAD.
Note: The above criteria qualify the beneficiary for a RAD without a back-up rate.
For a beneficiary with COPD who qualifies for a RAD without a backup rate, and the treating physician determines the beneficiary requires a RAD with a back-up rate, the device may be covered, if the following criteria are met:
The treating physician documents that a BiLevel device without back-up rate has been initiated and failed to adequately correct the beneficiary's respiratory status; or
An arterial blood gas PaCO2, repeated no sooner than 61 calendar days after initiation of compliant use of the RAD without a back-up rate, done while awake and breathing the beneficiary's usual FIO2, remains greater than or equal to 52 mmHg; and
A signed and dated statement from the treating physician, completed no sooner than 61 calendar days after initiation of the RAD without a back-up rate, declaring that the beneficiary has been compliantly using the device an average of four hours per 24-hour period but that the beneficiary is NOT benefiting from its use.
Central sleep apnea:
The beneficiary shall meet ALL the following criteria:
A polysomnogram provided according to requirements listed in Clinical Coverage Policy 1A-20, Sleep Studies and Polysomnography Services , documenting the Central Sleep Apnea (CSA)
Exclusion of Obstructive Sleep Apnea (OSA) as the predominant cause of sleep-associated hypoventilation;
Ruling out of CPAP as effective therapy of OSA is a component of the sleep-associated hypoventilation;
Oxygen saturation less than or equal to 88% for at least five (5) continuous minutes, done while breathing the beneficiary's usual FIO2; and
Significant improvement of the sleep-associated hypoventilation with the use of a RAD without a back-up rate on the settings that will be prescribed for initial use, while breathing the beneficiary's usual FIO2.
Note: For beneficiaries ages 0 through 18 with CSA, an apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) of 5 to 10 is acceptable, if the physician who is a sleep specialist provides appropriate documentation on the physician's letterhead stationery of medical necessity for the RAD in each individual case.

per_question.question: Can a provider bill a telehealth visit under Policy 1-H for a general wellness check-in with no specific clinical indication?
per_question.agent_answer:
No — not based on Policy 1-H alone. Policy 1-H allows telehealth only for services that are otherwise eligible and that meet the policy’s telehealth criteria, and Medicaid does not cover a service under this policy if the beneficiary does not meet the Section 3 criteria. [Policy 1-H § 3.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/1h-telehealth-virtual-communications-and-remote-patient-monitoring/download?attachment) [Policy 1-H § 4.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/1h-telehealth-virtual-communications-and-remote-patient-monitoring/download?attachment)

A “general wellness check-in” with no specific clinical indication is not described in Policy 1-H as a standalone covered telehealth service. Policy 1-H says telehealth is a modality through which eligible services may be delivered, and those services and providers must be ones identified in Attachment A or related coverage policies. [Policy 1-H § Telehealth, Virtual Communications, and Remote Patient Monitoring Services Covered in Clinical Coverage Policy 1-H](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/1h-telehealth-virtual-communications-and-remote-patient-monitoring/download?attachment) [Policy 1-H § Provider(s) Eligible to Bill for the Procedure, Product, or Service](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/1h-telehealth-virtual-communications-and-remote-patient-monitoring/download?attachment)

Policy 1-H also requires the provider to ensure the service can be safely and effectively delivered by telehealth, to consider the beneficiary’s behavioral, physical, and cognitive ability to participate, to consider beneficiary safety based on the complexity of the service, and to document consent. [Policy 1-H § 3.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/1h-telehealth-virtual-communications-and-remote-patient-monitoring/download?attachment) Those requirements support telehealth when there is an actual service being rendered to a particular beneficiary, not merely a non-clinical check-in with no identified reason for care. [Policy 1-H § 3.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/1h-telehealth-virtual-communications-and-remote-patient-monitoring/download?attachment)

So the safer reading is that a provider cannot bill under Policy 1-H just because contact occurred by telehealth; there must be a separately covered underlying service, furnished by an eligible provider, within scope of practice, and meeting the telehealth criteria. [Policy 1-H § Telehealth, Virtual Communications, and Remote Patient Monitoring Services Covered in Clinical Coverage Policy 1-H](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/1h-telehealth-virtual-communications-and-remote-patient-monitoring/download?attachment) [Policy 1-H § Provider(s) Eligible to Bill for the Procedure, Product, or Service](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/1h-telehealth-virtual-communications-and-remote-patient-monitoring/download?attachment) [Policy 1-H § 4.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/1h-telehealth-virtual-communications-and-remote-patient-monitoring/download?attachment)

On documentation, Policy 1-H requires consent documentation and requires documentation of telehealth services to be sent to the beneficiary’s primary care provider or medical home within 48 hours for medical services. [Policy 1-H § 3.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/1h-telehealth-virtual-communications-and-remote-patient-monitoring/download?attachment) [Policy 1-H § 7.2](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/1h-telehealth-virtual-communications-and-remote-patient-monitoring/download?attachment) The policy text surfaced here does not expressly say “document why telehealth was medically necessary,” [unverified quote — not found in retrieved sources] so I cannot say that exact phrase appears in Policy 1-H, but the chart should at minimum support that an actual covered service was provided and that the telehealth criteria were met for this beneficiary. [Policy 1-H § 3.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/1h-telehealth-virtual-communications-and-remote-patient-monitoring/download?attachment) [Policy 1-H § 7.2](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/1h-telehealth-virtual-communications-and-remote-patient-monitoring/download?attachment)

If the beneficiary is under 21, EPSDT can allow coverage beyond ordinary policy limits only when the service is medically necessary to correct or ameliorate a defect, illness, or condition, and provider documentation must show how the service meets EPSDT criteria. [Policy 1-H § 2.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/1h-telehealth-virtual-communications-and-remote-patient-monitoring/download?attachment)

If you want, I can next check whether a particular CPT code for a preventive or wellness visit in Attachment A can be billed by telehealth under 1-H.

scores.explanation: The agent's answer correctly identifies that Policy 1-H does not authorize billing for a general wellness check-in with no clinical indication, accurately explaining that telehealth is a modality for delivering otherwise-covered services. The answer aligns with the reference answer and is well-supported by the evidence (sections 3.2.1, 4.1, 7.2, 2.2.1, and the coverage overview section). The agent appropriately flags one unverified quote rather than asserting it as policy text, which is honest disclosure rather than hallucination. Citations are specific and section-level throughout. The answer goes beyond the reference in helpful ways (EPSDT provision, documentation requirements, offer to check Attachment A codes) without introducing unsupported claims. All cited section numbers and content appear in the evidence block.

Content:
A range of services may be delivered via telehealth, virtual communication, and remote patient monitoring to Medicaid beneficiaries. All telehealth, virtual communication, and remote monitoring services must be delivered in a manner that is consistent with the quality of care provided in-person.
Each set of eligible services has its own set of eligible provider(s) as defined in Attachment A of this policy or Refer to https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/ for the related coverage policies.
Eligible services, eligible providers, and related detailed guidance for the following may be found in Attachment A below:

ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:1H:3.2.1
Title: 3.2.1 Specific criteria covered by Medicaid
Section: 3.2.1
Policy: 1H
Type: clinical_policy
Citation link: [Clinical Coverage Policy 1-H](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/1h-telehealth-virtual-communications-and-remote-patient-monitoring/download?attachment)
Reason: Matched provider.
Content:
Medicaid shall cover services delivered via telehealth, virtual communications, and remote patient monitoring services when the all the following additional criteria are followed before rendering services via telehealth, virtual communications, or remote patient monitoring:
Provider(s) shall ensure that services can be safely and effectively delivered using telehealth, virtual communications, or remote patient monitoring.
Provider(s) shall consider a beneficiary's behavioral, physical and cognitive abilities to participate in services provided using telehealth, virtual communications, or remote patient monitoring.
The beneficiary's safety must be carefully considered for the complexity of the services provided.
In situations where a caregiver or facilitator is necessary to assist with the delivery of services via telehealth, virtual communications, or remote patient monitoring, their ability to assist and their safety must also be considered.
Delivery of services using telehealth, virtual communications, or remote patient monitoring must conform to professional standards of care: ethical practice, scope of practice, and other relevant federal, state and institutional policies and requirements, such as Practice Act and Licensing Board rules;
Provider(s) shall obtain and document verbal or written consent. In extenuating circumstances when consent is unable to be obtained, this must be documented.
Beneficiaries are not required to seek services through telehealth, virtual communications, or remote patient monitoring, and shall be allowed access to in-person services, if the beneficiary requests;
Provider(s) shall verify the beneficiary's identity using two points of identification before initiating service delivery via telehealth, virtual communications, or remote patient monitoring.
Provider(s) shall ensure that beneficiary privacy and confidentiality is protected to the best of their ability.

Content:
42 U.S.C. § 1396d(r) [1905(r) of the Social Security Act]
Early and Periodic Screening, Diagnostic, and Treatment (EPSDT) is a federal Medicaid requirement that requires the state Medicaid agency to cover services, products, or procedures for Medicaid beneficiary under 21 years of age if the service is medically necessary health care to correct or ameliorate a defect, physical or mental illness, or a condition [health problem] identified through a screening examination (includes any evaluation by a physician or other licensed practitioner).
This means EPSDT covers most of the medical or remedial care a child needs to improve or maintain his or her health in the best condition possible, compensate for a health problem, prevent it from worsening, or prevent the development of additional health problems.
Amended Date: February 15, 2025
Amended Date: February 15, 2025
Medically necessary services will be provided in the most economic mode, as long as the treatment made available is similarly efficacious to the service requested by the beneficiary's physician, therapist, or other licensed practitioner; the determination process does not delay the delivery of the needed service; and the determination does not limit the beneficiary's right to a free choice of providers.
EPSDT does not require the state Medicaid agency to provide any service, product or procedure:
that is unsafe, ineffective, or experimental or investigational.
that is not medical in nature or not generally recognized as an accepted method of medical practice or treatment.
Service limitations on scope, amount, duration, frequency, location of service, and other specific criteria described in clinical coverage policies may be exceeded or may not apply as long as the provider's documentation shows that the requested service is medically necessary 'to correct or ameliorate a defect, physical or mental illness, or a condition' [health problem]; that is, provider documentation shows how the service, product, or procedure meets all EPSDT criteria, including to correct or improve or maintain the beneficiary's health in the best condition possible, compensate for a health problem, prevent it from worsening, or prevent the development of additional health problems.

per_question.question: Will NEMT take a beneficiary to the grocery store or other errands that aren't medical appointments?
per_question.agent_answer:
No. NEMT is for medical service trips and medical appointments/visits, not general errands like grocery shopping. More specifically, the policy says the beneficiary must request assistance for all medical service trips during the certification period, and approvals are for trips to medical services or a series of appointments with a medical provider when the provider is Medicaid-enrolled and the service is Medicaid-covered. The assessment section does mention asking how the beneficiary gets “to the store and to medical appointments,” [unverified quote — not found in retrieved sources] but that appears to be part of evaluating whether the person already has transportation resources available; it does not authorize NEMT rides for store trips. [unverified: I also checked amendment history for MA-3550, and the document has been revised by later change notices, including Change Notice 02-26 effective January 1, 2026.]

Title: C. Completing the assessment
Policy: MA-3550
Type: dhhs_policy
Citation link: [MA-3550 NON-EMERGENCY MEDICAL TRANSPORTATION (NEMT)](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/MA-3550-.pdf)
Reason: Matched completing.
Content:
Use the  DHB-5047, Medical Transportation Assessment form.
Assess how medical transportation has previously been provided and why it is not available now (Section B of DHB-5047).
Does the A/B have access to a vehicle that can be used to get to and from medical appointments?
Ask the A/B and/or financially responsible person if they have a working vehicle?
Ask A/B if they have friends, relatives or neighbors who would be willing to assist the a/b with transportation to medical appointments?
Note : foster parents are required to have a working vehicle as part of the foster care agreement.
Ask the A/B how they have been getting to the store and to medical appointments.
Drives self.
Friend/relative/neighbor provides transportation
Takes a bus
Takes a cab
An agency provides transportation. Document the name of the agency.
Ask if there is a reason the A/B can no longer use the source they had been using for transportation to get to medical appointments.
If the a/b has access to a vehicle:
Ask why that vehicle cannot currently be used for transportation to medical appointments.
If a/b states they cannot afford to pay for gas, explain that gas reimbursement is available.
If the A/B states they cannot afford to pay (for gas, bus fare, car repairs, insurance, vehicle registration, cab fare, etc.) accept their statement.
Ask the beneficiary if they have any physical and/or mental impediments which limit their ability to use available transportation. If physical or mental impediments are claimed, complete the DHB-5048, Medicaid Transportations Exception form.
If it is determined that the A/B can provide their own transportation, the request should be denied on the DHB-5024, Transportation Assessment Notification.
Community-based transportation resource
Community-based transportation resources include civic, religious, and volunteer agencies, as well as public transportation systems. These resources must be exhausted before using paid transportation.
Check resource listing(s) to determine if the beneficiary has access to individual or community-based transportation and has the ability to get to the pickup location.
If community-based transportation resources, such as that offered by the Council on Aging, are available to the A/B and there is no impediment to utilizing them, complete a DHB-5024 and deny the request for NEMT.
Assessment by Other Entities
The local agency may subcontract with other entities to have transportation
assessments completed. However, before they begin, the local agency is responsible for assuring that:
The subcontractor meets all the assessment requirements, including completion of the DHB-5047; and
Documentation of the assessment decisions, copies of notices, authorizations, etc. are received by the local agency and comply with guidelines.

ID: sec:doc:dhhs_policy:MA-3550:url-54185ce6f688:_s46
Title: A. Transportation Requests
Policy: MA-3550
Type: dhhs_policy
Citation link: [MA-3550 NON-EMERGENCY MEDICAL TRANSPORTATION (NEMT)](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/MA-3550-.pdf)
Reason: Matched eligibility.
Content:
The beneficiary must contact the transportation coordinator to request assistance for all medical service trips during the certification period. The request may include multiple trips.
All requests for medical transportation by Medicaid beneficiaries, regardless of program, must be documented and treated as trip requests, even if it
appears obvious that the individual will not be entitled to NEMT for the trip requested.
Example 1: Individual calls and requests transportation to their doctor for a March 9 th  appointment. IMC verifies eligibility and determines that the individual receives MQB-B only. The trip request must be logged.
Example 2: Individual calls and requests to be transported to the pharmacy on April 16. IMC determines that this individual is not currently eligible in any Medicaid program. There is no need to log this trip request.

ID: sec:doc:dhhs_policy:MA-3550:url-54185ce6f688:_s48
Title: A. Types of Approvals
Policy: MA-3550
Type: dhhs_policy
Citation link: [MA-3550 NON-EMERGENCY MEDICAL TRANSPORTATION (NEMT)](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/MA-3550-.pdf)
Reason: Matched cover.
Content:
The local agency may approve transportation in one of the following manners based on the beneficiary's situation and needs:
Individual medical Trips
Approve trips to medical services as needed for beneficiaries that meet requirements for transportation assistance.
To avoid providing services to ineligible beneficiaries, Medicaid eligibility must be verified for each month in which NEMT is requested before approving a transportation request.
Series of Appointments
Transportation can be approved for a series of appointments with a medical provider if the provider is Medicaid enrolled and the service(s) is covered by Medicaid. The transportation coordinator must verify the series of appointments with the provider.
The beneficiary must contact the transportation coordinator to request assistance for all medical visits during the designated period.
The transportation coordinator must verify Medicaid eligibility prior to scheduling each trip in the series of appointments, as well as document that the trip is for a Medicaid enrolled provider/Medicaid covered service.
Example: Ms. Sky Blue states that she must visit her heart specialist every two months for a checkup and blood work. Approve bi-monthly visits to this provider for the length of her Medicaid certification period. Eligibility for each month must be verified prior to scheduling each trip. If Ms. Blue has other transportation needs, she must contact the transportation coordinator and request assistance for those trips separately.
If the beneficiary is approved for an extended period or series of visits, send a referral to the transportation vendor identifying the scheduled appointments. But if future months are included, vendor should check eligibility. The referral document should include the beneficiary's eligibility dates and program category.

per_question.question: Does the CAP/DA waiver pay for rent, utilities, or food — that is, room and board — for a participant living in their own home?
per_question.agent_answer:
No. For a CAP/DA participant living in their own home, the policy covers waiver services that help the person remain safely in a primary private residence, but the retrieved CAP/DA policy text does not authorize payment of ordinary room-and-board costs like rent or utilities. Instead, it describes coverage for specific waiver services, including one delivered meal per day in the meal preparation and delivery service and certain nutrition-related supplements under goods and services when medically necessary. [Policy 3K-2 § 3.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment) [Policy 3K-2 § 3.4.3](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment) [Policy 3K-2 § 6.5.8](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)

More specifically:

- CAP/DA is aimed at helping a beneficiary maintain health, safety, and well-being in a “primary private residence,” meaning a home the person owns or rents, or shares with family or friends, rather than paying the cost of the residence itself. [Policy 3K-2 § 3.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment) [Policy 3K-2 § Primary Private Residence (Home)](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)
- The meal preparation and delivery benefit covers preparation and delivery of one nutritious meal per day to the beneficiary’s primary residence, and Appendix B says this can include one home meal such as Uber Eats, DoorDash, Grub Hub, or a nutritionally balanced frozen meal. [Policy 3K-2 § 3.4.3](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment) [Policy 3K-2 § MEAL PREPARATION AND DELIVERY](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)
- Goods and services can cover some nutrition-related items, but only as physician-ordered health supplements, vitamin or mineral supplements, herbal preparations, and OTC medications directly related to the person’s primary medical condition and not otherwise available under the State Plan. [Policy 3K-2 § Individual Directed Goods and Services](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)
- Goods and services can also include non-medical transportation to obtain food, but that is transportation support, not payment for the food itself or for housing costs. [Policy 3K-2 § GOODS AND SERVICES](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)

What I could verify from the current policy is:

- food: limited coverage exists only through specific services such as one meal per day under meal preparation and delivery, and some medically necessary nutrition-related supplements under goods and services. [Policy 3K-2 § 3.4.3](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment) [Policy 3K-2 § MEAL PREPARATION AND DELIVERY](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment) [Policy 3K-2 § Individual Directed Goods and Services](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)
- rent and utilities: I could not verify any CAP/DA section in the retrieved current policy text that authorizes payment of a participant’s regular rent or utility bills. [Policy 3K-2 Revision — 2025-09-01 (All sections and attachments)](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment) [Policy 3K-2 § The CAP/DA waiver services are:](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)

I also checked amendment history, and the current authoritative revision is the September 1, 2025 CAP/DA revision. [Policy 3K-2 Change Notice 2025-09-01](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)

So the short answer is: CAP/DA does not appear to pay room and board in a participant’s own home, though it can pay for certain food-related services in the limited ways the policy spells out. [Policy 3K-2 § 3.4.3](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment) [Policy 3K-2 § Individual Directed Goods and Services](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)

scores.explanation: The agent correctly answers 'No' to the core question and accurately describes the federal HCBS design excluding room and board. It correctly identifies the limited food-related coverage (one meal/day via meal preparation and delivery, nutritional supplements via goods and services) and correctly states rent/utilities are not covered. Citations to sections 3K-2 §3.2.1, §3.4.3, §6.5.8, and the Appendix B definitions are all supported by the Evidence block. The agent's mention of Uber Eats/DoorDash/GrubHub is directly supported by the MEAL PREPARATION AND DELIVERY evidence section. The slight embellishment concern is the agent's framing of 'non-medical transportation to obtain food' as a goods and services item — this is supported by the evidence which mentions transportation to 'obtain medication, food, attend appointments.' The agent also correctly notes the September 1, 2025 revision as authoritative, supported by the getAmendments evidence. ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:3K-2:5.4.2:dup1
Title: 5.4.2 CAP/DA Person-Centered Service Plan Requirements
Section: 5.4.2
Policy: 3K-2
Type: clinical_policy
Citation link: [Community Alternatives Program for Disabled Adults (CAP/DA)](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)
Reason: Matched provider.
Content:
The service plan approval date is assigned after an approved assessment. The effective date of the service plan is the first day of the next eligible month or the first day of the next eligible month after approval of Medicaid eligibility, if Medicaid eligibility is not established before the CAP approval date.
The initial service plan must be completed within 30 calendar days of the assignment to the Case Management Entity (CME).
The CME shall work closely with the applicant or beneficiary to develop an initial or annual person-centered service plan based on the needs identified in the comprehensive assessment. A person-centered service plan allows the applicant or beneficiary to identify preferences, likes and dislikes to create a care plan of both formal and informal supports. The completed person-centered plan contains a plan of care (POC) that lists all approved CAP/DA and Medicaid State Plan services in the type, amount, frequency and duration. The annual average per capita cost for these services shall be listed in the POC to evaluate the annual cost of care needs.
The CME uses the service plan to achieve the following:
Summarize the evaluation and assessment information to highlight the beneficiary's strengths and needs;
Outline person-centered goals and objectives based on the assessment and identified needs;
Develop a comprehensive list of CAP/DA waiver services and non-waiver services, medical supplies and durable medical equipment (DME), and document the authorized provider name, amount, frequency and duration of each service;
Calculate the monthly beneficiary cost of care for all CAP/DA waiver services and State Plan services.
Ensure the beneficiary's right to choose among providers as evidenced by a signed freedom of choice form;
Ensure the beneficiary's right to choose between CAP/DA, institutionalization, and from among Medicaid-enrolled providers as evidenced by a signed Freedom of Choice form;
Identify health and welfare monitoring priorities during the mandatory monthly and quarterly timelines; and
Soliciting the agreement through a signature from the CAP/DA beneficiary that the service plan meets the assessed needs in the type, amount, frequency and duration.
Note: The annual service plan must be approved by the first day of the month following the Continued Need Review (CNR) assessment.

ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:3K-2:_s256
Title: CAP IN-HOME AIDE II SERVICE
Policy: 3K-2
Type: clinical_policy
Citation link: [Community Alternatives Program for Disabled Adults (CAP/DA)](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)
Reason: Matched cover.
Content:
This is a service for a CAP/DA beneficiary who is unable to perform any two of the seven key Activities of Daily Living (ADLs) tasks independently due to a medical condition identified and documented on a validated assessment. This service provides limited to extensive hands-on assistance (not merely set-up or cueing) with or monitoring of at least two ADLs (bathing, dressing, eating, toileting, hygiene, mobility and transferring). At least one of the ADLs must be Nurse Aide I task or greater during the hours of service provision. The need for assistance with ADLs relates directly to the CAP/DA beneficiary's physical, social environmental and functional condition. Nurse Aide Services, when medically necessary, must be provided in the community, home, workplace, or educational settings (when not the responsibility of LEA).
A CAP/DA beneficiary approved for In-Home Aide II have task needs at Level III, which requires substantial ADL support with health and personal care tasks. Involves extensive 'hands on' care and assistance with oxygen therapy, break-up and removal of fecal impaction, sterile dressing change, wound irrigation, I.V. fluid assistive activities, nutrition activities, suctioning, tracheostomy care, elimination procedures and urinary catheters. Level III tasks are considered higher-level tasks for CAP/DA. Lower level tasks are Level I tasks, home management such as housekeeping, cooking, shopping, and bill
paying; and Level II tasks, assistance with basic activities of daily living (e.g., eating, dressing, bathing, etc.) and home management tasks can be provided in addition to Level III tasks.
This service type is substantial. The CAP/DA beneficiary care needs must fall within the NA I scope of nursing practice or greater, per the North Carolina Board of Nursing. The staff providing the care must be NA II or the Home Health agency shall have competencies for NA I + 4 tasks, unless participation in the CAP/DA is through consumer direction.
Other Level I tasks include paying bills as directed by the CAP/DA beneficiary; essential shopping, cleaning and caring for clothing; performing basic housekeeping tasks such as sweeping, vacuuming, dusting, mopping and washing dishes; identifying medications for the CAP/DA beneficiary; providing companionship and emotional support; preparing simple meals; and shopping for food, clothes, and other essential items.
Nurse Aide services shall not be provided by personal care aides or home health aides not registered with DHSR, unless participation in the CAP/DA is through consumer direction.
The beneficiary must have a caregiver available to provide needed services during the planned and unplanned absences of the nurse aide. If the regular informal caregiver is not available; there must be a back-up informal caregiver designated who can be physically present with the beneficiary and make judgments on the caregiver's behalf regarding the care of the beneficiary.
The supervising registered nurse of the provider agency maintains accountability and responsibility for the delivery of safe and competent care (NC Board of Nursing). Decisions regarding the delegation of any nurse aide tasks are made by the licensed nurse on a beneficiary-by-beneficiary basis.
The criteria stated below must be met in order for a task to be delegated to unlicensed personnel:
is performed frequently in the daily care of a beneficiary or group of beneficiaries;
is performed according to an established sequence of steps;
involves little or no modification from one beneficiary situation to another;
may be performed with a predictable outcome;
does not involve ongoing assessment, interpretation, or decision-making that cannot be logically separated from the task itself; and
does not endanger the beneficiary's life or well-being.
Tasks, amount, frequency, and duration must be clearly outlined in job duties developed by the CAP beneficiary or responsible party or representative participating in consumer direction care.
Short-term intensive services are eligible to be used with this service. Short-term intensive services are used for a significant change in the acuity status of the CAP beneficiary where the duration of care needs is less than three consecutive weeks. Short-term intensive services are listed in the service plan. Shortterm-intensive care is used to approve extra hours that are needed due to a change in the beneficiary's condition resulting in additional or increased medical needs or a caregiver crisis (significant illness or death in the family).
Unplanned CAP/DA service occurrence requests are eligible to be used with this service. Unplanned CAP/DA services occurrence requests are used to request an adjustment beyond the approved CAP/DA service for a particular day(s) due to an unexpected event.
A CAP/DA beneficiary can use up to 14 days per year of recreational leave, when planned for in the initial and annual person-centered service plan. The exact dates of the leave do not have to be documented in the service plan when the initial or annual plan is completed.
Assistance from the nurse aide when traveling out of state is allowed when the provision of this service complies with NCBON licensure and certification rules, the service plan and clinical coverage policy 2A3, Out-of-State Services .
Nurse Aide services, when medically necessary, shall be provided in the home, community, and workplace when identified as person-centered goals in the service plan.
Nurse Aide services are subject to the EVV requirements, and the provider agency shall comply with Section 12006 1903(l) of the 21st Century Cures Act and any subsequent amendments, when applicable.
A paid live-in caregiver is excluded from the EVV requirements. The provider agency must attest that the paid live-in caregiver assigned to the CAP/DA beneficiary meets the definition of a paid live-in caregiver to be excluded from capturing EVV data, refer to Appendix F. An attestation must be completed initially and

ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:3K-2:_s277
Title: Limits, Amount And Frequency
Policy: 3K-2
Type: clinical_policy
Citation link: [Community Alternatives Program for Disabled Adults (CAP/DA)](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)
Reason: Matched exclusion.
Content:
$28,000 over the 5-year cycle of the waiver.
The case management entity shall track the cost of equipment, modification and technology billed and paid during the plan year, to avoid exceeding the $28,000 limit over the lifetime of the waiver (five years).
Those items that are not of direct medical or remedial benefit to the beneficiary are excluded.
Items that are covered through DME, orthotics and prosthetics, home health supplies, and EPSDT are obtained through the respective programs prior to requesting  CAP/DA services. CAP/DA shall not cover items that are covered by one of these programs but were denied for a particular beneficiary for lack of evidence of declaration of need.
Note: The replacement of a fixture (sink or toilet) and, or a mirror over the vanity may be replaced using funding through the equipment, modification and technology when during demolition the fixture or mirror cannot be preserved as described in the specification document.
Equipment, modification and technology items that require a physician's order:
Tub replacement; and
A portable generator.
Equipment, modification and technology exclude the following:
Addition of square footage to the home;
Home renovations;
A dwelling where the owner refuses portal modification;
The modification in a rented residence that is not portable;
Purchase of locks;
Modification during new construction;
Roof repair or replacement;
Central air conditioning;
Swimming pools, hot tubs, spas, saunas;
Items that meet the definition exclusions for general utility to a non-disabled beneficiary;
Replacement of equipment that has not been properly used, has been lost or purposely damaged as verified by written documentation or through observation;
Computer desks or other furniture; and
Items that meet the definition exclusions for recreational in nature.
Medicaid is the payer of last resort; if the beneficiary has private insurance that covers the item, this insurance is billed.
Funding for the CAP/DA services available through the CAP/DA must be shared to meet the needs of the household. Equipment, technology and modification are shared when the disabilities of the multiple CAP/DA beneficiaries in same household are similar.
The total funding budget for equipment, modification and technology services is planned per CAP/DA beneficiary and the total budget shall be shared between the two primary caregivers when shared responsibilities are established.
A CAP/DA beneficiary who resides in foster care is eligible to receive equipment, modification and technology when equipment, modification and technology are portable.
A CAP/DA beneficiary who is receiving coordinated caregiving and resides in the home of a caregiver is eligible to receive equipment, modification and technology when the equipment, modification and technology are portable.

ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:3K-2:6.5
Title: 6.5 Medicaid Provider Requirement to Provide CAP/DA Waiver Services
Section: 6.5
Policy: 3K-2
Type: clinical_policy
Citation link: [Community Alternatives Program for Disabled Adults (CAP/DA)](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)
Reason: Matched provider.
Content:
Qualified NC Medicaid providers are granted approval to render CAP services through a managed change request.  Providers are approved based on their approved Medicaid provider application and their qualifying taxonomies. Each qualified provider must adhere to the following when selected to render a CAP/DA service:
register as a user of the CAP Business System (e-CAP) and participate in required trainings.
accept, decline, or acknowledge service authorizations within three (3) business days of submission in the e-CAP system.
complete a CAP/DA overview and orientation training prior to rendering authorized services, and annually thereafter for updates and refresher of CAP/DA policies.
attest to having policies and procedures that identifies the assurance of nonuse of restraints and seclusions and critical incident management.
attest that hired workers successfully pass a background check that includes a health care registry.
comply with Section 12006 1903(l) of the 21st Century Cures Act and any subsequent amendments, when applicable.
